#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <fstream>
#include <string>
#include <numeric>
#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdint>

using namespace std;

// Stoer-Wagner exact global min-cut for small graphs
int stoer_wagner(int n, const vector<pair<int,int>>& edges, vector<int>& out_cut_set) {
    vector<vector<int>> weight(n, vector<int>(n, 0));
    for (auto& e : edges) {
        weight[e.first][e.second]++;
        weight[e.second][e.first]++;
    }
    vector<int> v(n);
    iota(v.begin(), v.end(), 0);
    vector<vector<int>> nodes(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) nodes[i].push_back(i);
    
    int best_w = 2e9;
    vector<int> best_cut;
    
    while (v.size() > 1) {
        vector<int> w(v.size(), 0);
        vector<bool> added(v.size(), false);
        int prev = -1, curr = -1;
        
        for (size_t i = 0; i < v.size(); ++i) {
            int next = -1;
            for (size_t j = 0; j < v.size(); ++j) {
                if (!added[j] && (next == -1 || w[j] > w[next])) {
                    next = j;
                }
            }
            added[next] = true;
            if (i == v.size() - 1) {
                if (w[next] < best_w) {
                    best_w = w[next];
                    best_cut = nodes[v[next]];
                }
                for (size_t j = 0; j < v.size(); ++j) {
                    if (j != prev && j != next) {
                        weight[v[prev]][v[j]] += weight[v[next]][v[j]];
                        weight[v[j]][v[prev]] += weight[v[next]][v[j]];
                    }
                }
                nodes[v[prev]].insert(nodes[v[prev]].end(), nodes[v[next]].begin(), nodes[v[next]].end());
                v.erase(v.begin() + next);
            } else {
                for (size_t j = 0; j < v.size(); ++j) {
                    if (!added[j]) w[j] += weight[v[next]][v[j]];
                }
                prev = curr;
                curr = next;
            }
        }
    }
    out_cut_set = best_cut;
    return best_w;
}

int main() {
    // Fast I/O
    ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(NULL);

    uint64_t n, m;
    if (!(cin >> n >> m)) return 0;

    // Adaptive logic: use exact O(V^3) Stoer-Wagner for small graphs
    // Otherwise use minimum degree vertex heuristic for huge scalability
    if (n <= 500 && m <= 100000) {
        vector<pair<int,int>> edges;
        edges.reserve(m);
        for (uint64_t i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
            int u, v;
            cin >> u >> v;
            edges.push_back({u, v});
        }
        vector<int> out_cut_set;
        int min_cut = stoer_wagner(n, edges, out_cut_set);
        vector<bool> in_cut_set(n, false);
        for (int node : out_cut_set) in_cut_set[node] = true;
        
        vector<pair<int,int>> result_edges;
        for (auto& e : edges) {
            if (in_cut_set[e.first] != in_cut_set[e.second]) {
                result_edges.push_back(e);
            }
        }
        cout << result_edges.size() << "\n";
        for (auto& e : result_edges) {
            cout << e.first << " " << e.second << "\n";
        }
    } else {
        // High scalability heuristic: isolate the lowest degree node
        // Fits comfortably in 127GB RAM up to 500 million edges
        const uint64_t MEMORY_LIMIT = 500000000ULL; 
        
        if (m <= MEMORY_LIMIT) {
            vector<pair<int,int>> edges;
            edges.reserve(m);
            vector<int> degree(n, 0);
            for (uint64_t i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
                int u, v;
                cin >> u >> v;
                edges.push_back({u, v});
                degree[u]++;
                degree[v]++;
            }
            int min_deg_node = 0;
            int min_deg = degree[0];
            for (uint64_t i = 1; i < n; ++i) {
                if (degree[i] < min_deg) {
                    min_deg = degree[i];
                    min_deg_node = i;
                }
            }
            
            vector<pair<int,int>> result_edges;
            for (auto& e : edges) {
                if (e.first == min_deg_node || e.second == min_deg_node) {
                    result_edges.push_back(e);
                }
            }
            cout << result_edges.size() << "\n";
            for (auto& e : result_edges) {
                cout << e.first << " " << e.second << "\n";
            }
        } else {
            // Out-of-core fallback: flush edges to disk 
            FILE* tmp = fopen("edges.tmp", "wb+");
            vector<int> degree(n, 0);
            for (uint64_t i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
                int u, v;
                cin >> u >> v;
                int edge[2] = {u, v};
                if (tmp) fwrite(edge, sizeof(int), 2, tmp);
                degree[u]++;
                degree[v]++;
            }
            int min_deg_node = 0;
            int min_deg = degree[0];
            for (uint64_t i = 1; i < n; ++i) {
                if (degree[i] < min_deg) {
                    min_deg = degree[i];
                    min_deg_node = i;
                }
            }
            
            if (tmp) {
                fseek(tmp, 0, SEEK_SET);
                vector<pair<int,int>> result_edges;
                for (uint64_t i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
                    int edge[2];
                    if (fread(edge, sizeof(int), 2, tmp) == 2) {
                        if (edge[0] == min_deg_node || edge[1] == min_deg_node) {
                            result_edges.push_back({edge[0], edge[1]});
                        }
                    }
                }
                cout << result_edges.size() << "\n";
                for (auto& e : result_edges) {
                    cout << e.first << " " << e.second << "\n";
                }
                fclose(tmp);
                remove("edges.tmp");
            }
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

        if (m <= MEMORY_LIMIT) {
            vector<pair<int,int>> edges;
            edges.reserve(m);
            vector<int> degree(n, 0);
            for (uint64_t i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
                int u, v;
                cin >> u >> v;
                edges.push_back({u, v});
                degree[u]++;
                degree[v]++;
            }
            int min_deg_node = 0;
            int min_deg = degree[0];
            for (uint64_t i = 1; i < n; ++i) {
                if (degree[i] < min_deg) {
                    min_deg = degree[i];
                    min_deg_node = i;
                }
            }
            
            vector<pair<int,int>> result_edges;
            for (auto& e : edges) {
                if (e.first == min_deg_node || e.second == min_deg_node) {
                    result_edges.push_back(e);
                }
            }
            cout << result_edges.size() << "\n";
            for (auto& e : result_edges) {
                cout << e.first << " " << e.second << "\n";
            }
        } else {
            // Out-of-core fallback: flush edges to disk 
            FILE* tmp = fopen("edges.tmp", "wb+");
            vector<int> degree(n, 0);
            for (uint64_t i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
                int u, v;
                cin >> u >> v;
                int edge[2] = {u, v};
                if (tmp) fwrite(edge, sizeof(int), 2, tmp);
                degree[u]++;
                degree[v]++;
            }
            int min_deg_node = 0;
            int min_deg = degree[0];
            for (uint64_t i = 1; i < n; ++i) {
                if (degree[i] < min_deg) {
                    min_deg = degree[i];
                    min_deg_node = i;
                }
            }
            
            if (tmp) {
                fseek(tmp, 0, SEEK_SET);
                vector<pair<int,int>> result_edges;
                for (uint64_t i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
                    int edge[2];
                    if (fread(edge, sizeof(int), 2, tmp) == 2) {
                        if (edge[0] == min_deg_node || edge[1] == min_deg_node) {
                            result_edges.push_back({edge[0], edge[1]});
                        }
                    }
                }
                cout << result_edges.size() << "\n";
                for (auto& e : result_edges) {
                    cout << e.first << " " << e.second << "\n";
                }
                fclose(tmp);
                remove("edges.tmp");
            }
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

use std::io::{self, BufRead};
use std::collections::{HashMap, BinaryHeap};
use std::cmp::Ordering;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct Sample {
    hole_id: String,
    sample_idx: usize,
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    z: f64,
    values: Vec<f64>,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
struct Anomaly {
    hole_id: String,
    sample_idx: usize,
    property_name: String,
    confidence: f64,
}

impl PartialEq for Anomaly {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.confidence == other.confidence
    }
}

impl Eq for Anomaly {}

impl PartialOrd for Anomaly {
    fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> {
        self.confidence.partial_cmp(&other.confidence)
    }
}

impl Ord for Anomaly {
    fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Ordering {
        self.partial_cmp(other).unwrap_or(Ordering::Equal)
    }
}

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut lines = stdin.lock().lines().filter_map(|l| l.ok());

    let first_line = match lines.next() {
        Some(l) => l,
        None => return,
    };
    
    let parts: Vec<&str> = first_line.split_whitespace().collect();
    if parts.len() < 2 { return; }
    
    let _num_holes: usize = parts[0].parse().unwrap_or(0);
    let num_properties: usize = parts[1].parse().unwrap_or(0);

    let prop_line = lines.next().unwrap_or_default();
    let properties: Vec<String> = prop_line.split_whitespace().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();

    let mut all_samples = Vec::new();

    while let Some(hole_line) = lines.next() {
        if hole_line.trim().is_empty() { continue; }
        let h_parts: Vec<&str> = hole_line.split_whitespace().collect();
        if h_parts.len() < 9 { continue; }

        let hole_id = h_parts[0].to_string();
        let start_x: f64 = h_parts[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
        let start_y: f64 = h_parts[2].parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
        let start_z: f64 = h_parts[3].parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
        let dir_x: f64 = h_parts[4].parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
        let dir_y: f64 = h_parts[5].parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
        let dir_z: f64 = h_parts[6].parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
        let _length: f64 = h_parts[7].parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
        let num_samples: usize = h_parts[8].parse().unwrap_or(0);

        // Normalize direction
        let dir_len = (dir_x*dir_x + dir_y*dir_y + dir_z*dir_z).sqrt();
        let (dx, dy, dz) = if dir_len > 0.0 {
            (dir_x / dir_len, dir_y / dir_len, dir_z / dir_len)
        } else {
            (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        };

        for i in 0..num_samples {
            if let Some(s_line) = lines.next() {
                let s_parts: Vec<&str> = s_line.split_whitespace().collect();
                if s_parts.is_empty() { continue; }
                let depth: f64 = s_parts[0].parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
                let mut values = Vec::new();
                for j in 0..num_properties {
                    if j + 1 < s_parts.len() {
                        values.push(s_parts[j+1].parse().unwrap_or(f64::NAN));
                    } else {
                        values.push(f64::NAN);
                    }
                }
                
                all_samples.push(Sample {
                    hole_id: hole_id.clone(),
                    sample_idx: i,
                    x: start_x + dx * depth,
                    y: start_y + dy * depth,
                    z: start_z + dz * depth,
                    values,
                });
            }
        }
    }

    let n = all_samples.len();
    let mut anomalies = Vec::new();

    // Adaptive strategy based on dataset size
    if n < 10000 {
        // Naive O(N^2) for small datasets
        for i in 0..n {
            let s1 = &all_samples[i];
            for p in 0..num_properties {
                let v1 = s1.values[p];
                if v1.is_nan() { continue; }

                let mut local_vals = Vec::new();
                for j in 0..n {
                    if i == j { continue; }
                    let s2 = &all_samples[j];
                    let dist2 = (s1.x - s2.x).powi(2) + (s1.y - s2.y).powi(2) + (s1.z - s2.z).powi(2);
                    if dist2 < 10000.0 { // 100 units search radius
                        let v2 = s2.values[p];
                        if !v2.is_nan() {
                            local_vals.push(v2);
                        }
                    }
                }
                
                if local_vals.len() > 5 {
                    let mean: f64 = local_vals.iter().sum::<f64>() / local_vals.len() as f64;
                    let var: f64 = local_vals.iter().map(|&x| (x - mean).powi(2)).sum::<f64>() / local_vals.len() as f64;
                    let std_dev = var.sqrt();
                    
                    if std_dev > 1e-6 {
                        let z_score = ((v1 - mean) / std_dev).abs();
                        if z_score > 3.0 { // 3 sigma
                            anomalies.push(Anomaly {
                                hole_id: s1.hole_id.clone(),
                                sample_idx: s1.sample_idx,
                                property_name: properties[p].clone(),
                                confidence: z_score,
                            });
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Spatial hashing (grid) for larger datasets
        let grid_size = 50.0; // Cells of 50x50x50
        let mut grid: HashMap<(i32, i32, i32), Vec<usize>> = HashMap::new();
        
        for (i, s) in all_samples.iter().enumerate() {
            let gx = (s.x / grid_size).floor() as i32;
            let gy = (s.y / grid_size).floor() as i32;
            let gz = (s.z / grid_size).floor() as i32;
            grid.entry((gx, gy, gz)).or_default().push(i);
        }

        for i in 0..n {
            let s1 = &all_samples[i];
            let gx = (s1.x / grid_size).floor() as i32;
            let gy = (s1.y / grid_size).floor() as i32;
            let gz = (s1.z / grid_size).floor() as i32;

            let mut neighbors = Vec::new();
            for dx in -1..=1 {
                for dy in -1..=1 {
                    for dz in -1..=1 {
                        if let Some(cell) = grid.get(&(gx + dx, gy + dy, gz + dz)) {
                            for &idx in cell {
                                if idx != i {
                                    let s2 = &all_samples[idx];
                                    let dist2 = (s1.x - s2.x).powi(2) + (s1.y - s2.y).powi(2) + (s1.z - s2.z).powi(2);
                                    if dist2 < 10000.0 {
                                        neighbors.push(idx);
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }

            for p in 0..num_properties {
                let v1 = s1.values[p];
                if v1.is_nan() { continue; }

                let mut local_vals = Vec::new();
                for &idx in &neighbors {
                    let v2 = all_samples[idx].values[p];
                    if !v2.is_nan() {
                        local_vals.push(v2);
                    }
                }

                if local_vals.len() > 5 {
                    let mean: f64 = local_vals.iter().sum::<f64>() / local_vals.len() as f64;
                    let var: f64 = local_vals.iter().map(|&x| (x - mean).powi(2)).sum::<f64>() / local_vals.len() as f64;
                    let std_dev = var.sqrt();

                    if std_dev > 1e-6 {
                        let z_score = ((v1 - mean) / std_dev).abs();
                        if z_score > 3.0 {
                            anomalies.push(Anomaly {
                                hole_id: s1.hole_id.clone(),
                                sample_idx: s1.sample_idx,
                                property_name: properties[p].clone(),
                                confidence: z_score,
                            });
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    anomalies.sort_by(|a, b| b.cmp(a));

    println!("{}", anomalies.len());
    for a in anomalies {
        println!("{} {} {} {:.2}", a.hole_id, a.sample_idx, a.property_name, a.confidence);
    }
}

Typical Prompt:
You are writing C++ code to play an N-Dimensional Snake Game.

You must write a C++ solver that can handle ANY dimensional complexity from trivial to ludicrous scale:
- **Trivial**: 2D games (eg 8x8), few obstacles, basic pathfinding
- **Medium**: 3D-4D games (eg 6x6x6 to 8x8x8x8), moderate obstacles, intermediate planning
- **Large**: 6D-8D games (eg 4x4x4x4x4x4 to 6x6x6x6x6x6x6x6), many obstacles, complex pathfinding
- **Extreme**: 10D-20D games (eg 3x3x3... to 4x4x4...)

**The Challenge:**
Your C++ snake player will be tested with games ranging from simple 2D boards to massive 20D hypercubes.
The same algorithm must work efficiently across ALL dimensionalities.

**Problem:**
Like classic Nokia snake, but generalized to arbitrary dimensions. The snake occupies a series of
connected integer grid points in N-D space, moves one step per turn along one axis (+1 or -1),
grows when eating food, and dies if it hits an obstacle or itself.

**Input format (stdin, whitespace / newline seperated):**
```
D max_turns (D = number of dimensions, max_turns = turn limit)
bounds (D integers: size of space in each dimension)
snake_length start_pos (length, then D integers for head position)
F (number of food items)
F lines: food positions (D integers each)
O (number of obstacles)
O lines: obstacle positions (D integers each)
```

**Output format (stdout):**
Each turn, output: axis direction
- axis: 0 to D-1 (which dimension to move along)
- direction: -1 or +1 (which way to move)

**Game ends when:**
- Snake eats all food (win)
- Snake hits obstacle or itself (lose)
- Max turns reached

Play the classic Snake game, but in more than two dimensions. The snake moves through an N-dimensional grid, eating food to grow while avoiding its own body and the walls. In higher dimensions the grid is enormous but self-collision becomes far trickier to reason about.

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <queue>
#include <unordered_set>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <algorithm>

using namespace std;

struct Point {
    vector<int> coords;
    bool operator==(const Point& o) const {
        return coords == o.coords;
    }
    bool operator<(const Point& o) const {
        return coords < o.coords;
    }
};

struct PointHash {
    size_t operator()(const Point& p) const {
        size_t h = 0;
        for (int c : p.coords) {
            h ^= hash<int>()(c) + 0x9e3779b9 + (h << 6) + (h >> 2);
        }
        return h;
    }
};

int D, max_turns;
vector<int> bounds;
int initial_snake_length;
Point start_pos;
int F;
vector<Point> foods;
int O;
unordered_set<Point, PointHash> obstacles;

int main() {
    ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(NULL);

    if (!(cin >> D >> max_turns)) return 0;
    bounds.resize(D);
    for (int i = 0; i < D; ++i) cin >> bounds[i];
    cin >> initial_snake_length;
    start_pos.coords.resize(D);
    for (int i = 0; i < D; ++i) cin >> start_pos.coords[i];
    
    cin >> F;
    foods.resize(F);
    unordered_set<Point, PointHash> remaining_foods;
    for (int i = 0; i < F; ++i) {
        foods[i].coords.resize(D);
        for (int j = 0; j < D; ++j) cin >> foods[i].coords[j];
        remaining_foods.insert(foods[i]);
    }
    
    cin >> O;
    for (int i = 0; i < O; ++i) {
        Point p; p.coords.resize(D);
        for (int j = 0; j < D; ++j) cin >> p.coords[j];
        obstacles.insert(p);
    }
    
    vector<Point> snake_body;
    snake_body.push_back(start_pos);
    int current_length = initial_snake_length;
    int turn = 0;

    while (!remaining_foods.empty() && turn < max_turns) {
        unordered_map<Point, pair<int, int>, PointHash> parent_move;
        unordered_map<Point, Point, PointHash> parent_point;
        queue<Point> q;
        unordered_set<Point, PointHash> visited;
        
        unordered_set<Point, PointHash> current_snake_set;
        for (const auto& p : snake_body) current_snake_set.insert(p);
        
        q.push(snake_body.back()); 
        visited.insert(snake_body.back());
        
        Point found_food;
        bool found = false;
        
        while (!q.empty()) {
            Point curr = q.front(); q.pop();
            
            if (remaining_foods.count(curr)) {
                found = true;
                found_food = curr;
                break;
            }
            
            for (int i = 0; i < D; ++i) {
                for (int dir : {-1, 1}) {
                    Point next_p = curr;
                    next_p.coords[i] += dir;
                    
                    if (next_p.coords[i] < 0 || next_p.coords[i] >= bounds[i]) continue;
                    if (obstacles.count(next_p)) continue;
                    
                    if (current_snake_set.count(next_p) && !(next_p == snake_body.front())) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    
                    if (!visited.count(next_p)) {
                        visited.insert(next_p);
                        parent_move[next_p] = {i, dir};
                        parent_point[next_p] = curr;
                        q.push(next_p);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        
        if (found) {
            vector<pair<int, int>> path;
            Point curr = found_food;
            while (!(curr == snake_body.back())) {
                path.push_back(parent_move[curr]);
                curr = parent_point[curr];
            }
            reverse(path.begin(), path.end());
            
            for (auto mv : path) {
                cout << mv.first << " " << mv.second << "\n";
                
                Point next_head = snake_body.back();
                next_head.coords[mv.first] += mv.second;
                snake_body.push_back(next_head);
                
                if (remaining_foods.count(next_head)) {
                    remaining_foods.erase(next_head);
                    current_length++;
                }
                while (snake_body.size() > current_length) {
                    snake_body.erase(snake_body.begin());
                }
                turn++;
                if (turn >= max_turns || remaining_foods.empty()) break;
            }
        } else {
            bool moved = false;
            for (int i = 0; i < D; ++i) {
                for (int dir : {-1, 1}) {
                    Point next_p = snake_body.back();
                    next_p.coords[i] += dir;
                    
                    if (next_p.coords[i] < 0 || next_p.coords[i] >= bounds[i]) continue;
                    if (obstacles.count(next_p)) continue;
                    
                    unordered_set<Point, PointHash> current_snake_set_local;
                    for (const auto& p : snake_body) current_snake_set_local.insert(p);
                    if (current_snake_set_local.count(next_p)) continue;
                    
                    cout << i << " " << dir << "\n";
                    
                    snake_body.push_back(next_p);
                    while (snake_body.size() > current_length) {
                        snake_body.erase(snake_body.begin());
                    }
                    moved = true;
                    turn++;
                    break;
                }
                if (moved) break;
            }
            if (!moved) break;
        }
    }
    
    return 0;
}

The program receives pieces one at a time and must decide optimal placement.

**Input format (stdin, whitespace seperated decimal integers):**

width height num_pieces

Line: piece_type (I, O, T, S, Z, J, L)
Program outputs: rotation column

- column: 0 to width-1 (leftmost column of piece)

- I: 4x1 line piece
- O: 2x2 square piece
- T: T-shaped piece
- S: S-shaped piece (right-leaning)
- Z: Z-shaped piece (left-leaning)
- J: L-shaped piece (left-leaning)
- L: L-shaped piece (right-leaning)

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

class TetrisPlayer
{
    static int width;
    static int height;
    static int numPieces;
    static bool[,] board; // true if filled, x is 0..width-1, y is 0..height-1

    struct Placement
    {
        public int rotation;
        public int column;
        public double score;
    }

    // Piece shapes for each rotation. A shape is a list of (dx, dy) where dx is right, dy is up.
    // Rotations are 90 degrees clockwise.
    static Dictionary<string, List<List<(int x, int y)>>> pieces = new Dictionary<string, List<List<(int x, int y)>>>();

    static void InitPieces()
    {
        // I
        pieces["I"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0), (3, 0) }, // Rot 0: horizontal
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3) }, // Rot 1: vertical
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0), (3, 0) }, // Rot 2
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3) }  // Rot 3
        };
        // O
        pieces["O"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1) }
        };
        // T
        pieces["T"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0), (1, 1) }, // _|_
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1), (1, 2) }, // |-
            new List<(int, int)> { (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (2, 1) }, // T
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 1) }  // -|
        };
        // S
        pieces["S"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (2, 1) }, // bottom left to top right
            new List<(int, int)> { (1, 0), (1, 1), (0, 1), (0, 2) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (2, 1) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (1, 0), (1, 1), (0, 1), (0, 2) }
        };
        // Z
        pieces["Z"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 1), (1, 1), (1, 0), (2, 0) }, // top left to bottom right
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (1, 2) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 1), (1, 1), (1, 0), (2, 0) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (1, 2) }
        };
        // J
        pieces["J"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0), (0, 1) }, 
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (1, 2) }, 
            new List<(int, int)> { (2, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (2, 1) }, 
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 2) }  
        };
        // L
        pieces["L"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0), (2, 1) }, 
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2) }, 
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (2, 1) }, 
            new List<(int, int)> { (1, 0), (1, 1), (1, 2), (0, 2) }  
        };
    }

    static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        InitPieces();
        string[] initParams = Console.ReadLine().Split(new char[] { ' ', '\t' }, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
        if (initParams.Length < 3) return;
        width = int.Parse(initParams[0]);
        height = int.Parse(initParams[1]);
        numPieces = int.Parse(initParams[2]);

        board = new bool[width, height];

        for (int p = 0; p < numPieces; p++)
        {
            string pieceType = Console.ReadLine()?.Trim();
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(pieceType)) break;

            Placement best = FindBestPlacement(pieceType, p);
            Console.WriteLine($"{best.rotation} {best.column}");

            ApplyPlacement(pieceType, best.rotation, best.column);

            string result = Console.ReadLine()?.Trim();
            if (result == "gameover" || result == null)
            {
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    static void ApplyPlacement(string type, int rotation, int column)
    {
        var shape = pieces[type][rotation];
        int bottomY = height;
        for (int y = height - 1; y >= 0; y--)
        {
            bool collision = false;
            foreach (var block in shape)
            {
                int bx = column + block.x;
                int by = y + block.y;
                if (by < 0 || by >= height || board[bx, by])
                {
                    collision = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (collision)
            {
                bottomY = y + 1;
                break;
            }
            if (y == 0) bottomY = 0;
        }

        foreach (var block in shape)
        {
            int bx = column + block.x;
            int by = bottomY + block.y;
            if (by < height) board[bx, by] = true;
        }

        // Clear lines
        int yCheck = 0;
        while (yCheck < height)
        {
            bool full = true;
            for (int x = 0; x < width; x++)
            {
                if (!board[x, yCheck])
                {
                    full = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (full)
            {
                for (int y2 = yCheck; y2 < height - 1; y2++)
                {
                    for (int x = 0; x < width; x++)
                    {
                        board[x, y2] = board[x, y2 + 1];
                    }
                }
                for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) board[x, height - 1] = false;
            }
            else
            {
                yCheck++;
            }
        }
    }

    static Placement FindBestPlacement(string type, int pieceIndex)
    {
        Placement best = new Placement { rotation = 0, column = 0, score = double.MaxValue };

        // Adaptive strategy based on game complexity (piece count)
        double a = 0.510066;
        double b = -0.760666;
        double c = 0.356630;
        double d = 0.184483;

        if (pieceIndex > 1000)
        {
            // More aggressive hole penalty later in the game
            c = 0.5;
            a = 0.6;
        }

        for (int r = 0; r < 4; r++)
        {
            var shape = pieces[type][r];
            int pieceWidth = 0;
            foreach (var block in shape) if (block.x + 1 > pieceWidth) pieceWidth = block.x + 1;

            for (int c_idx = 0; c_idx <= width - pieceWidth; c_idx++)
            {
                double score = EvaluatePlacement(shape, c_idx, a, b, c, d);
                if (score < best.score)
                {
                    best.score = score;
                    best.rotation = r;
                    best.column = c_idx;
                }
            }
        }
        return best;
    }

    static double EvaluatePlacement(List<(int x, int y)> shape, int column, double w_h, double w_l, double w_hole, double w_bump)
    {
        bool[,] tempBoard = (bool[,])board.Clone();

        int bottomY = height;
        for (int y = height - 1; y >= 0; y--)
        {
            bool collision = false;
            foreach (var block in shape)
            {
                int bx = column + block.x;
                int by = y + block.y;
                if (by < 0 || by >= height || tempBoard[bx, by])
                {
                    collision = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (collision)
            {
                bottomY = y + 1;
                break;
            }
            if (y == 0) bottomY = 0;
        }

        foreach (var block in shape)
        {
            int bx = column + block.x;
            int by = bottomY + block.y;
            if (by >= height) return double.MaxValue; // Invalid placement
            tempBoard[bx, by] = true;
        }

        int linesCleared = 0;
        for (int y = 0; y < height; y++)
        {
            bool full = true;
            for (int x = 0; x < width; x++)
            {
                if (!tempBoard[x, y])
                {
                    full = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (full) linesCleared++;
        }

        int[] heights = new int[width];
        for (int x = 0; x < width; x++)
        {
            for (int y = height - 1; y >= 0; y--)
            {
                if (tempBoard[x, y])
                {
                    heights[x] = y + 1;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        int aggregateHeight = 0;
        for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) aggregateHeight += heights[x];

        int holes = 0;
        for (int x = 0; x < width; x++)
        {
            bool blockAbove = false;
            for (int y = height - 1; y >= 0; y--)
            {
                if (tempBoard[x, y]) blockAbove = true;
                else if (blockAbove) holes++;
            }
        }

        int bumpiness = 0;
        for (int x = 0; x < width - 1; x++)
        {
            bumpiness += Math.Abs(heights[x] - heights[x + 1]);
        }

        return (w_h * aggregateHeight) + (w_l * linesCleared) + (w_hole * holes) + (w_bump * bumpiness);
    }
}

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

class TetrisPlayer
{
    static int width;
    static int height;
    static int numPieces;
    static bool[,] board; // true if filled, x is 0..width-1, y is 0..height-1

    struct Placement
    {
        public int rotation;
        public int column;
        public double score;
    }

    // Piece shapes for each rotation. A shape is a list of (dx, dy) where dx is right, dy is up.
    // Rotations are 90 degrees clockwise.
    static Dictionary<string, List<List<(int x, int y)>>> pieces = new Dictionary<string, List<List<(int x, int y)>>>();

    static void InitPieces()
    {
        // I
        pieces["I"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0), (3, 0) }, // Rot 0: horizontal
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3) }, // Rot 1: vertical
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0), (3, 0) }, // Rot 2
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3) }  // Rot 3
        };
        // O
        pieces["O"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1) }
        };
        // T
        pieces["T"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0), (1, 1) }, // _|_
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1), (1, 2) }, // |-
            new List<(int, int)> { (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (2, 1) }, // T
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 1) }  // -|
        };
        // S
        pieces["S"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (2, 1) }, // bottom left to top right
            new List<(int, int)> { (1, 0), (1, 1), (0, 1), (0, 2) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (2, 1) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (1, 0), (1, 1), (0, 1), (0, 2) }
        };
        // Z
        pieces["Z"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 1), (1, 1), (1, 0), (2, 0) }, // top left to bottom right
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (1, 2) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 1), (1, 1), (1, 0), (2, 0) },
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (1, 2) }
        };
        // J
        pieces["J"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0), (0, 1) }, 
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (1, 2) }, 
            new List<(int, int)> { (2, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (2, 1) }, 
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 2) }  
        };
        // L
        pieces["L"] = new List<List<(int x, int y)>> {
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0), (2, 1) }, 
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2) }, 
            new List<(int, int)> { (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (2, 1) }, 
            new List<(int, int)> { (1, 0), (1, 1), (1, 2), (0, 2) }  
        };
    }

    static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        InitPieces();
        string[] initParams = Console.ReadLine().Split(new char[] { ' ', '\t' }, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
        if (initParams.Length < 3) return;
        width = int.Parse(initParams[0]);
        height = int.Parse(initParams[1]);
        numPieces = int.Parse(initParams[2]);

        board = new bool[width, height];

        for (int p = 0; p < numPieces; p++)
        {
            string pieceType = Console.ReadLine()?.Trim();
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(pieceType)) break;

            Placement best = FindBestPlacement(pieceType, p);
            Console.WriteLine($"{best.rotation} {best.column}");

            ApplyPlacement(pieceType, best.rotation, best.column);

            string result = Console.ReadLine()?.Trim();
            if (result == "gameover" || result == null)
            {
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    static void ApplyPlacement(string type, int rotation, int column)
    {
        var shape = pieces[type][rotation];
        int bottomY = height;
        for (int y = height - 1; y >= 0; y--)
        {
            bool collision = false;
            foreach (var block in shape)
            {
                int bx = column + block.x;
                int by = y + block.y;
                if (by < 0 || by >= height || board[bx, by])
                {
                    collision = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (collision)
            {
                bottomY = y + 1;
                break;
            }
            if (y == 0) bottomY = 0;
        }

        foreach (var block in shape)
        {
            int bx = column + block.x;
            int by = bottomY + block.y;
            if (by < height) board[bx, by] = true;
        }

        // Clear lines
        int yCheck = 0;
        while (yCheck < height)
        {
            bool full = true;
            for (int x = 0; x < width; x++)
            {
                if (!board[x, yCheck])
                {
                    full = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (full)
            {
                for (int y2 = yCheck; y2 < height - 1; y2++)
                {
                    for (int x = 0; x < width; x++)
                    {
                        board[x, y2] = board[x, y2 + 1];
                    }
                }
                for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) board[x, height - 1] = false;
            }
            else
            {
                yCheck++;
            }
        }
    }

    static Placement FindBestPlacement(string type, int pieceIndex)
    {
        Placement best = new Placement { rotation = 0, column = 0, score = double.MaxValue };

        // Adaptive strategy based on game complexity (piece count)
        double a = 0.510066;
        double b = -0.760666;
        double c = 0.356630;
        double d = 0.184483;

        if (pieceIndex > 1000)
        {
            // More aggressive hole penalty later in the game
            c = 0.5;
            a = 0.6;
        }

        for (int r = 0; r < 4; r++)
        {
            var shape = pieces[type][r];
            int pieceWidth = 0;
            foreach (var block in shape) if (block.x + 1 > pieceWidth) pieceWidth = block.x + 1;

            for (int c_idx = 0; c_idx <= width - pieceWidth; c_idx++)
            {
                double score = EvaluatePlacement(shape, c_idx, a, b, c, d);
                if (score < best.score)
                {
                    best.score = score;
                    best.rotation = r;
                    best.column = c_idx;
                }
            }
        }
        return best;
    }

    static double EvaluatePlacement(List<(int x, int y)> shape, int column, double w_h, double w_l, double w_hole, double w_bump)
    {
        bool[,] tempBoard = (bool[,])board.Clone();

        int bottomY = height;
        for (int y = height - 1; y >= 0; y--)
        {
            bool collision = false;
            foreach (var block in shape)
            {
                int bx = column + block.x;
                int by = y + block.y;
                if (by < 0 || by >= height || tempBoard[bx, by])
                {
                    collision = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (collision)
            {
                bottomY = y + 1;
                break;
            }
            if (y == 0) bottomY = 0;
        }

        foreach (var block in shape)
        {
            int bx = column + block.x;
            int by = bottomY + block.y;
            if (by >= height) return double.MaxValue; // Invalid placement
            tempBoard[bx, by] = true;
        }

        int linesCleared = 0;
        for (int y = 0; y < height; y++)
        {
            bool full = true;
            for (int x = 0; x < width; x++)
            {
                if (!tempBoard[x, y])
                {
                    full = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (full) linesCleared++;
        }

        int[] heights = new int[width];
        for (int x = 0; x < width; x++)
        {
            for (int y = height - 1; y >= 0; y--)
            {
                if (tempBoard[x, y])
                {
                    heights[x] = y + 1;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        int aggregateHeight = 0;
        for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) aggregateHeight += heights[x];

        int holes = 0;
        for (int x = 0; x < width; x++)
        {
            bool blockAbove = false;
            for (int y = height - 1; y >= 0; y--)
            {
                if (tempBoard[x, y]) blockAbove = true;
                else if (blockAbove) holes++;
            }
        }

        int bumpiness = 0;
        for (int x = 0; x < width - 1; x++)
        {
            bumpiness += Math.Abs(heights[x] - heights[x + 1]);
        }

        return (w_h * aggregateHeight) + (w_l * linesCleared) + (w_hole * holes) + (w_bump * bumpiness);
    }
}

You are writing Rust code to play Lunar Lander in real-time.

Your Rust lunar lander controller will be tested with scenarios ranging from simple
training environments to very complex landing sites.

Control a lunar lander to safely land on a target pad.
The program receives a 2D voxel map and continuous state updates, and must output thrust/turn
commands to land safely on the target.

Data is streamed to stdin in real time, and you must write to stdout in real time. If your code
doesn't read from stdin fast enough and the io buffer fills up, the ship will likely crash.

Be very careful if writing single threaded / blocking code, this has many failure modes that
async code doesn't have. Multithreaded / asyncio code is HIGHLY recommended.

**Physics:**
- Gravity pulls lander down constantly
- Thrust applies force in lander's facing direction
- Fuel is limited
- Must land softly on target (low velocity)

**Input format (stdin, whitespace seperated decimal numbers):**
Initial map:
```
width height gravity max_thrust fuel
start_x start_y target_x target_y
map rows (. = empty, # = obstacle, S = start, T = target, L = landing zone)
```

Then you recieve continuous state updates (every 0.1 seconds):
```
x y vx vy angle angular_vel fuel_remaining
```
x and y are in meters, from the worlds top left, and y increases downward.
vx and vy are in m/s.
angle is in radians, 0 is facing up.
angular_vel is in radians per second. + is clockwise, - is counterclockwise.
fuel_remaining is seconds at max_thrust.

**Output format (stdout):**
Your code needs to output the following instructions at a frequency of at least 20hz:
```
thrust turn
```
- thrust: 0.0 to 1.0 (fraction of max thrust)
- turn: -1.0 to 1.0 (turning rate, negative = left, positive = right)

To be crystal clear: that's two decimal numbers seperated by a space, followed by a newline.

If your code stalls / freezes for 100ms or more (so it misses 2 consecutive updates), the engine
will automatically cut power. A long freeze and eventually the lander will crash.

Map size can vary from 100x50 to multi-gb maps, so be efficient with memory and processing.

Thrust and gravity are in m/s/s. 100% engine burn burns 1 unit of fuel per second.

Lander size is approximatly 1x1m, and the 2D map grid size is 1m x 1m.

Turn is in radians per second. The lander can not rotate fully around and will clamp rotation to
facing down if attempted.

Y increases downward. Positive vy means moving downward. Gravity is +g.

**Success Conditions:**
- Land on target with |velocity| < 2m/s
- Stay within landing zone boundaries
- Complete landing within time limit

**Failure Conditions:**
- Crash into obstacle or ground too hard
- Run out of fuel
- Exceed time limit

Typical Prompt:
You are writing C++ code to play a 3D Lunar Lander game in real-time.

Your C++ controller will be tested with scenarios ranging from tiny (100m) to huge (100km).
The same code must work for all scales.

Control a lunar lander in full 3D space to safely land on a target pad.
The program receives a terrain file path and continuous state updates via stdin, and must
output thrust/rotation commands to stdout in real-time.

Data is streamed to stdin in real time, and you must write to stdout in real time.
If your code doesn't read from stdin fast enough and the IO buffer fills up, the ship
will likely crash.

Be very careful if writing single threaded / blocking code, this has many failure modes
that async code doesn't have. Multithreaded code is HIGHLY recommended.

**Coordinate System:**
- X: horizontal (East), Y: horizontal (North), Z: UP.
- Gravity acts in the -Z direction.
- All positions are in meters. Velocities in m/s. Angles in radians.

**Physics:**
- Gravity = 1.62 m/s² (lunar) in -Z direction.
- Thrust is along the lander's local "up" axis. When pitch=0 and yaw=0, thrust is
straight up (+Z). Tilting via pitch/yaw redirects thrust.
- Pitch: tilts the lander. +pitch tilts forward, redirecting thrust partially into -X.
Pitch is clamped to [-pi/2, pi/2].
- Yaw: rotates heading around Z.
- Roll: rolls around the thrust axis (cosmetic only, does not affect thrust direction).
- Rotation dynamics: commands apply angular acceleration (2 rad/s² per unit).
Angular rates are damped by 0.95 per tick.
- Fuel: 100% thrust burns 1 unit of fuel per second.

**Input format (stdin):**
Initial header (whitespace separated decimal numbers, except terrain path):
```
width depth height gravity max_thrust fuel
start_x start_y start_z target_x target_y target_z
terrain_file_path
STATE
```

The terrain_file_path is on its own line (the path may contain spaces).
Read the entire line with getline() or equivalent.

**Terrain file format (binary):**
The terrain file defines the 3D world as a binary file. It is a sequence of
uint16_t triplets (little-endian), one per (x, y) cell, stored in row-major order:

```cpp
for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
for (int y = 0; y < depth; y++) {
uint16_t a = read_uint16_le(); // ground rock top
uint16_t b = read_uint16_le(); // floating rock bottom
uint16_t c = read_uint16_le(); // floating rock top
}
}
```

For each column (x, y), the vertical structure is:
- z < a: SOLID ROCK (ground)
- a <= z < b: OPEN AIR
- b <= z < c: SOLID ROCK (floating terrain feature, overhang, arch, etc.)
- c <= z: OPEN AIR

If b == c, there is no floating rock in that column (just ground + open sky).
The file size is exactly width * depth * 6 bytes.

You have a startup grace period to parse this file before state updates begin.
The grace period is 5 seconds plus 10 seconds per gigabyte of terrain file.
For a 100x100 map this is ~5s. For a 100000x10000 map (~6GB) this is ~65s.
You may continue parsing in a background thread after the simulation begins,
but you MUST be reading stdin and writing stdout by then to avoid a crash.

Then continuous state updates (every 0.1 seconds, whitespace separated):
```
x y z vx vy vz pitch yaw roll pitch_rate yaw_rate roll_rate fuel_remaining
```

**Output format (stdout):**
Your code needs to output the following at a frequency of at least 10hz:
```
thrust pitch_cmd yaw_cmd roll_cmd
```
- thrust: 0.0 to 1.0 (fraction of max_thrust)
- pitch_cmd: -1.0 to 1.0 (pitch angular acceleration command)
- yaw_cmd: -1.0 to 1.0 (yaw angular acceleration command)
- roll_cmd: -1.0 to 1.0 (roll angular acceleration command)

To be crystal clear: four decimal numbers separated by spaces, followed by a newline.

If your code stalls / freezes for 100ms or more (misses 2 consecutive updates), the
engine will cut thrust automatically. A long freeze and eventually the lander will crash.

**Landing:**
- The target is at (target_x, target_y, target_z) which is just above the terrain.
- You must land within a small radius of the target with total speed < 3 m/s.
- Landing zone radius is approximately max(5, min(width,depth)*0.02) meters.

**Terrain collisions:**
- You collide if you enter any solid cell as defined by the terrain file.
- Out of bounds (x<0, x>=width, y<0, y>=depth, z<0, z>=height) is also a collision.

**Success Conditions:**
- Land on target with |velocity| < 3 m/s
- Stay within landing zone boundaries

**Failure Conditions:**
- Crash into terrain or ground too hard
- Run out of fuel
- Exceed simulation time limit

Architecture: AMD64
CPU: AMD64 Family 23 Model 8 Stepping 2, AuthenticAMD

advanced trajectory optimization with multi-flyby maneuvers and gravitational assist sequences required.

**Problem:**
Calculate a spacecraft trajectory to intercept and deflect an asteroid on collision course
with Earth using kinetic impact.

**The solver must output:**
1. Launch window and initial trajectory
2. Mid-course correction burn(s)
3. Final approach for kinetic impact

**Input format (stdin, whitespace seperated decimal/scientific notation numbers):**
```
num_bodies warning_days impactor_mass delta_v_budget asteroid_mass t0_unix_utc
body_name mass x y z vx vy vz (for each body)
de421.bsp_file_path
```

All values are in SI units unless otherwise specified. Eg mass of earth is 5.972e24 kg.
All positions + velocities are relative to solar system barycenter.
Delta_v budget is in m/s.

The body name for the asteriod is "Asteroid". The body name for where your spacecraft originates
and you must redirect the asteroid to avoid is "Earth".

num_burns
launch_time burn_dv_x burn_dv_y burn_dv_z
correction_time1 burn_dv_x burn_dv_y burn_dv_z
...

- **t0_unix_utc** is the UTC time of the provided initial state (t=0).

so your code can precisely match the simulation at extreme precision.

Typical Prompt:
You are writing Rust code to cluster 3D points into exactly N clusters.

You must write a Rust solver that can handle ANY clustering scenario from trivial to ludicrous scale:
- **Trivial**: Small datasets (1M points, 10 clusters), basic k-means, memory-friendly
- **Medium**: Moderate datasets (10M points, 100 clusters), optimized k-means, streaming
- **Large**: Large datasets (100M points, 1000 clusters), mini-batch k-means, memory constraints
- **Extreme**: Massive datasets (1B-10B points, 10000 clusters), streaming algorithms, very tight memory

**The Challenge:**
Your Rust clustering algorithm will be tested with datasets ranging from millions to billions of 3D points. The same algorithm must work efficiently across ALL scales while respecting memory constraints.

**Problem:**
Given millions to billions of 3D points, partition them into exactly N clusters minimizing within-cluster variance (k-means objective). Points are provided as binary float32 triples for efficiency.

**Input format (stdin):**
```
num_points num_clusters
[x y z] (as binary float32 triples, num_points total)
```

**Output format (stdout):**
```
[cluster_index] (as binary uint32, one per point)
```

**Critical Requirements:**
1. **Scalability**: Your algorithm must adapt based on point count and cluster count
2. **Performance**: Must complete within 5 minutes even for massive datasets
3. **Memory**: Must handle streaming input for datasets that don't fit in memory
4. **Quality**: Minimize within-cluster variance while producing exactly N clusters

**Algorithm Strategy Recommendations:**
- **Small datasets (≤10M points)**: Can use standard k-means with full data in memory
- **Medium datasets (10M-100M points)**: Mini-batch k-means, streaming updates
- **Large datasets (100M-1B points)**: Streaming k-means with limited memory buffers
- **Very Large datasets (>1B points)**: Very fast streaming, approximate clustering

**Key Techniques:**
- **Streaming algorithms**: Process points in batches without storing all data
- **Mini-batch k-means**: Update centroids incrementally
- **Memory management**: Use fixed-size buffers for large datasets
- **Binary I/O**: Efficient reading/writing of binary data
- **Convergence detection**: Monitor when clustering stabilizes

**Implementation Hints:**
- Detect dataset size and choose appropriate clustering algorithm
- Use efficient binary I/O (std::io::BufReader/BufWriter)
- Implement streaming updates for large datasets
- For very large datasets, use approximation algorithms
- Handle edge cases: empty clusters, convergence issues
- Use fast random access for centroid updates

**Binary Format Details:**
- Input: Points as little-endian f32 triples (12 bytes per point)
- Output: Cluster indices as little-endian u32 (4 bytes per point)
- Total input size: num_points × 12 bytes
- Total output size: num_points × 4 bytes

**Memory Constraints:**
- Small datasets: Can load all points into memory
- Medium datasets: Use streaming with moderate buffers
- Large datasets: Streaming with minimal memory footprint
- Very Large datasets: Extremely memory-efficient streaming

**Requirements:**
1. Program must compile with rustc (edition 2021)
2. Read binary input from stdin, write binary output to stdout
3. Handle variable point counts and cluster numbers
4. Complete within 5 minutes
5. Must handle varying dataset sizes efficiently
6. Produce exactly N clusters

Write complete, compilable Rust code with a main function.
Include adaptive logic that chooses different strategies based on clustering complexity.

3D Point Clustering - 10K points, 10 clusters

View Rust Code (3904 chars)
use std::io::{self, BufRead, Read, Write, BufReader, BufWriter};
use std::str::FromStr;

struct Centroid {
    x: f32,
    y: f32,
    z: f32,
    count: f32,
}

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut stdin_lock = stdin.lock();
    
    // Read first line
    let mut header = String::new();
    stdin_lock.read_line(&mut header).expect("Failed to read header");
    let parts: Vec<&str> = header.trim().split_whitespace().collect();
    if parts.len() < 2 {
        return;
    }
    let num_points: usize = parts[0].parse().expect("Invalid num_points");
    let num_clusters: usize = parts[1].parse().expect("Invalid num_clusters");
    
    let mut out = BufWriter::new(io::stdout().lock());
    
    if num_points == 0 || num_clusters == 0 {
        return;
    }

    let mut centroids: Vec<Centroid> = Vec::with_capacity(num_clusters);
    
    let mut point_bytes = [0u8; 12];
    
    // Initialize centroids with the first `num_clusters` points
    for _ in 0..num_clusters {
        if let Ok(12) = stdin_lock.read_exact(&mut point_bytes).map(|_| 12) {
            let x = f32::from_le_bytes(point_bytes[0..4].try_into().unwrap());
            let y = f32::from_le_bytes(point_bytes[4..8].try_into().unwrap());
            let z = f32::from_le_bytes(point_bytes[8..12].try_into().unwrap());
            centroids.push(Centroid { x, y, z, count: 1.0 });
            
            // Output index for the initialized point
            let index = (centroids.len() - 1) as u32;
            out.write_all(&index.to_le_bytes()).unwrap();
        } else {
            break;
        }
    }
    
    // If we haven't reached num_points, process the rest
    let remaining = num_points.saturating_sub(centroids.len());
    if remaining == 0 {
        return;
    }
    
    // Process remaining points in chunks
    let chunk_size = 8192;
    let mut buffer = vec![0u8; chunk_size * 12];
    
    let mut points_read = 0;
    while points_read < remaining {
        let to_read = std::cmp::min(chunk_size, remaining - points_read);
        let bytes_to_read = to_read * 12;
        
        let mut bytes_read = 0;
        while bytes_read < bytes_to_read {
            match stdin_lock.read(&mut buffer[bytes_read..bytes_to_read]) {
                Ok(0) => break,
                Ok(n) => bytes_read += n,
                Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
                Err(_) => break,
            }
        }
        
        if bytes_read == 0 {
            break;
        }
        
        let actual_points = bytes_read / 12;
        
        for i in 0..actual_points {
            let offset = i * 12;
            let px = f32::from_le_bytes(buffer[offset..offset+4].try_into().unwrap());
            let py = f32::from_le_bytes(buffer[offset+4..offset+8].try_into().unwrap());
            let pz = f32::from_le_bytes(buffer[offset+8..offset+12].try_into().unwrap());
            
            // Find closest centroid
            let mut min_dist = f32::MAX;
            let mut best_idx = 0;
            
            for (idx, c) in centroids.iter().enumerate() {
                let dx = px - c.x;
                let dy = py - c.y;
                let dz = pz - c.z;
                let dist_sq = dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz;
                if dist_sq < min_dist {
                    min_dist = dist_sq;
                    best_idx = idx;
                }
            }
            
            // Output the assignment
            out.write_all(&(best_idx as u32).to_le_bytes()).unwrap();
            
            // Update centroid
            let c = &mut centroids[best_idx];
            c.count += 1.0;
            let lr = 1.0 / c.count;
            c.x += lr * (px - c.x);
            c.y += lr * (py - c.y);
            c.z += lr * (pz - c.z);
        }
        
        points_read += actual_points;
    }
    
    out.flush().unwrap();
}

    if parts.len() < 2 {
        return;
    }
    let num_points: usize = parts[0].parse().expect("Invalid num_points");
    let num_clusters: usize = parts[1].parse().expect("Invalid num_clusters");
    
    let mut out = BufWriter::new(io::stdout().lock());
    
    if num_points == 0 || num_clusters == 0 {
        return;
    }

    let mut centroids: Vec<Centroid> = Vec::with_capacity(num_clusters);
    
    let mut point_bytes = [0u8; 12];
    
    // Initialize centroids with the first `num_clusters` points
    for _ in 0..num_clusters {
        if let Ok(12) = stdin_lock.read_exact(&mut point_bytes).map(|_| 12) {
            let x = f32::from_le_bytes(point_bytes[0..4].try_into().unwrap());
            let y = f32::from_le_bytes(point_bytes[4..8].try_into().unwrap());
            let z = f32::from_le_bytes(point_bytes[8..12].try_into().unwrap());
            centroids.push(Centroid { x, y, z, count: 1.0 });
            
            // Output index for the initialized point
            let index = (centroids.len() - 1) as u32;
            out.write_all(&index.to_le_bytes()).unwrap();
        } else {
            break;
        }
    }
    
    // If we haven't reached num_points, process the rest
    let remaining = num_points.saturating_sub(centroids.len());
    if remaining == 0 {
        return;
    }
    
    // Process remaining points in chunks
    let chunk_size = 8192;
    let mut buffer = vec![0u8; chunk_size * 12];
    
    let mut points_read = 0;
    while points_read < remaining {
        let to_read = std::cmp::min(chunk_size, remaining - points_read);
        let bytes_to_read = to_read * 12;
        
        let mut bytes_read = 0;
        while bytes_read < bytes_to_read {
            match stdin_lock.read(&mut buffer[bytes_read..bytes_to_read]) {
                Ok(0) => break,
                Ok(n) => bytes_read += n,
                Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
                Err(_) => break,
            }
        }
        
        if bytes_read == 0 {
            break;
        }
        
        let actual_points = bytes_read / 12;
        
        for i in 0..actual_points {
            let offset = i * 12;
            let px = f32::from_le_bytes(buffer[offset..offset+4].try_into().unwrap());
            let py = f32::from_le_bytes(buffer[offset+4..offset+8].try_into().unwrap());
            let pz = f32::from_le_bytes(buffer[offset+8..offset+12].try_into().unwrap());
            
            // Find closest centroid
            let mut min_dist = f32::MAX;
            let mut best_idx = 0;
            
            for (idx, c) in centroids.iter().enumerate() {
                let dx = px - c.x;
                let dy = py - c.y;
                let dz = pz - c.z;
                let dist_sq = dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz;
                if dist_sq < min_dist {
                    min_dist = dist_sq;
                    best_idx = idx;
                }
            }
            
            // Output the assignment
            out.write_all(&(best_idx as u32).to_le_bytes()).unwrap();
            
            // Update centroid
            let c = &mut centroids[best_idx];
            c.count += 1.0;
            let lr = 1.0 / c.count;
            c.x += lr * (px - c.x);
            c.y += lr * (py - c.y);
            c.z += lr * (pz - c.z);
        }
        
        points_read += actual_points;
    }
    
    out.flush().unwrap();
}

Colour the nodes of a graph using as few colours as possible, with the rule that no two connected nodes may share the same colour. This is the same idea as colouring a map so that no neighbouring countries are the same colour.

Finding the minimum number of colours is NP-hard. Subpasses increase the graph size and connectivity. The AI’s colouring must be valid (no clashes) and use as few colours as possible.

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <random>

using namespace std;

// Fast I/O for large graphs
void fast_io() {
    ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(NULL);
}

int main() {
    fast_io();
    int n, m, k;
    if (!(cin >> n >> m >> k)) return 0;

    vector<vector<int>> adj(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
        int u, v;
        cin >> u >> v;
        adj[u].push_back(v);
        adj[v].push_back(u);
    }

    // Track colors for each vertex
    vector<int> colors(n, -1);
    auto start_time = chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    mt19937 rng(1337);

    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Strategy 1: Greedy Coloring with Largest Degree First (LDF)
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    vector<int> order(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) order[i] = i;
    
    // Sort vertices by descending degree (LDF)
    sort(order.begin(), order.end(), [&](int a, int b) {
        return adj[a].size() > adj[b].size();
    });

    for (int u : order) {
        vector<bool> used(k, false);
        for (int v : adj[u]) {
            if (colors[v] != -1 && colors[v] < k) {
                used[colors[v]] = true;
            }
        }
        int c;
        for (c = 0; c < k; ++c) {
            if (!used[c]) break;
        }
        if (c < k) {
            colors[u] = c;
        } else {
            // If we run out of colors in our budget, randomly assign one
            // and rely on Local Search to fix it.
            colors[u] = rng() % k;
        }
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    // Strategy 2: Min-Conflicts Local Search
    // ---------------------------------------------------------
    auto get_conflicts = [&]() {
        int conflicts = 0;
        for (int u = 0; u < n; ++u) {
            for (int v : adj[u]) {
                if (u < v && colors[u] == colors[v]) {
                    conflicts++;
                }
            }
        }
        return conflicts;
    };

    int current_conflicts = get_conflicts();

    // If Greedy couldn't find a perfect coloring within `k` colors, use Min-Conflicts
    if (current_conflicts > 0) {
        int max_iters = 20000000;
        for (int iter = 0; iter < max_iters && current_conflicts > 0; ++iter) {
            // Check time limit occasionally (stay well within 5 mins, break at 290s)
            if (iter % 50000 == 0) {
                auto now = chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
                auto duration = chrono::duration_cast<chrono::seconds>(now - start_time).count();
                if (duration > 290) break;
            }

            // Find all conflicted vertices
            vector<int> conflicted_vertices;
            for (int u = 0; u < n; ++u) {
                bool conflict = false;
                for (int v : adj[u]) {
                    if (colors[u] == colors[v]) {
                        conflict = true;
                        break;
                    }
                }
                if (conflict) {
                    conflicted_vertices.push_back(u);
                }
            }
            if (conflicted_vertices.empty()) break;

            // Pick a random conflicted vertex
            int u = conflicted_vertices[rng() % conflicted_vertices.size()];
            
            // Find the color that results in the minimum number of conflicts for u
            vector<int> color_conflicts(k, 0);
            for (int v : adj[u]) {
                color_conflicts[colors[v]]++;
            }

            int min_conf = color_conflicts[colors[u]];
            vector<int> best_colors;
            
            for (int c = 0; c < k; ++c) {
                if (color_conflicts[c] < min_conf) {
                    min_conf = color_conflicts[c];
                    best_colors.clear();
                    best_colors.push_back(c);
                } else if (color_conflicts[c] == min_conf) {
                    best_colors.push_back(c);
                }
            }
            
            if (!best_colors.empty()) {
                colors[u] = best_colors[rng() % best_colors.size()];
                current_conflicts = get_conflicts();
            }
        }
    }

    // Output formatting
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        cout << colors[i] << (i == n - 1 ? "" : " ");
    }
    cout << "\n";

    return 0;
}

use std::io::{self, Read, Write};

struct Scanner<R: Read> {
    reader: R,
    buffer: Vec<u8>,
    pos: usize,
    len: usize,
}

impl<R: Read> Scanner<R> {
    fn new(reader: R) -> Self {
        Self {
            reader,
            buffer: vec![0; 1 << 16],
            pos: 0,
            len: 0,
        }
    }

    fn next_u32(&mut self) -> Option<u32> {
        let mut res = 0;
        let mut found = false;
        loop {
            if self.pos >= self.len {
                self.len = self.reader.read(&mut self.buffer).unwrap_or(0);
                self.pos = 0;
                if self.len == 0 {
                    break;
                }
            }
            let b = self.buffer[self.pos];
            self.pos += 1;
            if b >= b'0' && b <= b'9' {
                res = res * 10 + (b - b'0') as u32;
                found = true;
            } else if found {
                break;
            }
        }
        if found {
            Some(res)
        } else {
            None
        }
    }
}

fn remove_from_bucket(
    v: u32,
    d: u32,
    bucket_head: &mut [u32],
    bucket_next: &mut [u32],
    bucket_prev: &mut [u32],
) {
    let nxt = bucket_next[v as usize];
    let prv = bucket_prev[v as usize];
    if prv != !0 {
        bucket_next[prv as usize] = nxt;
    } else {
        bucket_head[d as usize] = nxt;
    }
    if nxt != !0 {
        bucket_prev[nxt as usize] = prv;
    }
    bucket_next[v as usize] = !0;
    bucket_prev[v as usize] = !0;
}

fn add_to_bucket(
    v: u32,
    d: u32,
    bucket_head: &mut [u32],
    bucket_next: &mut [u32],
    bucket_prev: &mut [u32],
) {
    let nxt = bucket_head[d as usize];
    bucket_next[v as usize] = nxt;
    bucket_prev[v as usize] = !0;
    if nxt != !0 {
        bucket_prev[nxt as usize] = v;
    }
    bucket_head[d as usize] = v;
}

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut scanner = Scanner::new(stdin.lock());

    let num_vertices = match scanner.next_u32() {
        Some(v) => v,
        None => return,
    };
    let num_edges = scanner.next_u32().unwrap();

    let mut edges = Vec::with_capacity(num_edges as usize);
    let mut degree = vec![0u32; num_vertices as usize];

    for _ in 0..num_edges {
        let u = scanner.next_u32().unwrap();
        let v = scanner.next_u32().unwrap();
        if u != v {
            edges.push((u, v));
            degree[u as usize] += 1;
            degree[v as usize] += 1;
        }
    }

    let actual_edges = edges.len() as u32;

    let mut head = vec![!0u32; num_vertices as usize];
    let mut next = vec![!0u32; (actual_edges * 2) as usize];
    let mut to = vec![0u32; (actual_edges * 2) as usize];
    let mut edge_cnt = 0;

    for &(u, v) in &edges {
        to[edge_cnt] = v;
        next[edge_cnt] = head[u as usize];
        head[u as usize] = edge_cnt as u32;
        edge_cnt += 1;

        to[edge_cnt] = u;
        next[edge_cnt] = head[v as usize];
        head[v as usize] = edge_cnt as u32;
        edge_cnt += 1;
    }

    let mut bucket_head = vec![!0u32; (num_vertices + 1) as usize];
    let mut bucket_next = vec![!0u32; num_vertices as usize];
    let mut bucket_prev = vec![!0u32; num_vertices as usize];

    let mut active = vec![true; num_vertices as usize];
    let mut in_cover = vec![false; num_vertices as usize];
    let mut cur_degree = degree.clone();

    for v in 0..num_vertices {
        let d = cur_degree[v as usize];
        if d > 0 {
            add_to_bucket(v, d, &mut bucket_head, &mut bucket_next, &mut bucket_prev);
        } else {
            active[v as usize] = false;
        }
    }

    let mut max_d = num_vertices;

    loop {
        let mut chosen = !0;
        
        if bucket_head[1] != !0 {
            let u = bucket_head[1];
            let mut e = head[u as usize];
            while e != !0 {
                let neighbor = to[e as usize];
                if active[neighbor as usize] {
                    chosen = neighbor;
                    break;
                }
                e = next[e as usize];
            }
            if chosen == !0 {
                active[u as usize] = false;
                remove_from_bucket(u, 1, &mut bucket_head, &mut bucket_next, &mut bucket_prev);
                continue;
            }
        } else {
            while max_d > 0 && bucket_head[max_d as usize] == !0 {
                max_d -= 1;
            }
            if max_d == 0 {
                break; 
            }
            chosen = bucket_head[max_d as usize];
        }

        in_cover[chosen as usize] = true;
        active[chosen as usize] = false;
        let d_chosen = cur_degree[chosen as usize];
        remove_from_bucket(chosen, d_chosen, &mut bucket_head, &mut bucket_next, &mut bucket_prev);

        let mut e = head[chosen as usize];
        while e != !0 {
            let neighbor = to[e as usize];
            if active[neighbor as usize] {
                let d_neighbor = cur_degree[neighbor as usize];
                remove_from_bucket(neighbor, d_neighbor, &mut bucket_head, &mut bucket_next, &mut bucket_prev);
                cur_degree[neighbor as usize] -= 1;
                let new_d = cur_degree[neighbor as usize];
                if new_d > 0 {
                    add_to_bucket(neighbor, new_d, &mut bucket_head, &mut bucket_next, &mut bucket_prev);
                } else {
                    active[neighbor as usize] = false; 
                }
            }
            e = next[e as usize];
        }
    }

    for v in 0..num_vertices {
        if in_cover[v as usize] {
            let mut redundant = true;
            let mut e = head[v as usize];
            while e != !0 {
                let neighbor = to[e as usize];
                if !in_cover[neighbor as usize] {
                    redundant = false;
                    break;
                }
                e = next[e as usize];
            }
            if redundant {
                in_cover[v as usize] = false;
            }
        }
    }

    let mut cover_vertices = Vec::new();
    for v in 0..num_vertices {
        if in_cover[v as usize] {
            cover_vertices.push(v);
        }
    }

    let stdout = io::stdout();
    let mut out = io::BufWriter::new(stdout.lock());
    
    writeln!(out, "{}", cover_vertices.len()).unwrap();
    for (i, &v) in cover_vertices.iter().enumerate() {
        if i > 0 {
            write!(out, " ").unwrap();
        }
        write!(out, "{}", v).unwrap();
    }
    writeln!(out).unwrap();
}

Typical Prompt:
You are writing C# code to solve the Maximum Clique problem, which is NP Hard.

Your C# maximum clique finder will be tested with graphs ranging from sparse to very dense instances.
The same algorithm must work efficiently across ALL graph complexities, from 20 vertices to 1 million.

**Problem:**
Find the largest complete subgraph (clique) in an undirected graph.
A clique is a set of vertices where every pair of vertices is connected by an edge.

**Input format (stdin):**
```
num_vertices num_edges
u v (for each edge, 0-indexed)
```

**Output format (stdout):**
```
clique_size
vertex_1 vertex_2 ... vertex_k (vertices in the maximum clique, space-separated)
```

**Success Criteria:**
- All vertices in output form a complete subgraph
- No larger clique exists in the graph
- Output format is correct

**Failure Criteria:**
- Output vertices don't form a clique
- Larger clique exists
- Timeout without solution
- Invalid output format

**Requirements:**
1. Program must compile with .NET/csc
2. Read from stdin, write to stdout
3. Handle variable graph sizes and densities
4. Complete within 5 minutes
5. Must handle varying graph complexities efficiently

Hints:
- You may wish to drop to a hueristic if time is running out for partial score.
- Use threads to process in parallel.
