using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;

class FastScanner {
    private System.IO.Stream stream;
    private byte[] buffer = new byte[1024 * 1024];
    private int head = 0;
    private int tail = 0;

    public FastScanner() {
        stream = System.Console.OpenStandardInput();
    }

    public int NextInt() {
        int c = Read();
        while (c <= 32) {
            if (c == -1) return -1;
            c = Read();
        }
        int res = 0;
        while (c > 32) {
            res = res * 10 + c - '0';
            c = Read();
        }
        return res;
    }

    private int Read() {
        if (head >= tail) {
            head = 0;
            tail = stream.Read(buffer, 0, buffer.Length);
            if (tail == 0) return -1;
        }
        return buffer[head++];
    }
}

class Graph {
    public HashSet<int> Vertices = new HashSet<int>();
    public Dictionary<int, HashSet<int>> InEdges = new Dictionary<int, HashSet<int>>();
    public Dictionary<int, HashSet<int>> OutEdges = new Dictionary<int, HashSet<int>>();

    public void AddVertex(int v) {
        if (Vertices.Add(v)) {
            InEdges[v] = new HashSet<int>();
            OutEdges[v] = new HashSet<int>();
        }
    }

    public void AddEdge(int u, int v) {
        OutEdges[u].Add(v);
        InEdges[v].Add(u);
    }

    public void RemoveVertex(int v) {
        if (!Vertices.Contains(v)) return;
        foreach (var u in InEdges[v]) OutEdges[u].Remove(v);
        foreach (var w in OutEdges[v]) InEdges[w].Remove(v);
        InEdges.Remove(v);
        OutEdges.Remove(v);
        Vertices.Remove(v);
    }

    public void RemoveEdge(int u, int v) {
        OutEdges[u].Remove(v);
        InEdges[v].Remove(u);
    }

    public Graph Copy() {
        Graph g = new Graph();
        foreach (var v in Vertices) {
            g.AddVertex(v);
        }
        foreach (var v in Vertices) {
            foreach (var w in OutEdges[v]) {
                g.AddEdge(v, w);
            }
        }
        return g;
    }
}

                    outEdgesList[v] = G.OutEdges[v].ToList();
                    edgeIndex[v] = 0;
                }

                while (idx < list.Count) {

                    if (!visited.Contains(w)) {
                        edgeIndex[v] = idx;
                        stack.Push(w);

            stack.Push(startNode);

                        stack.Push(w);
                    }
                }

            sccs.Add(scc);
        }

        return sccs;

                    if (!G.Vertices.Contains(v)) continue;
                    
                    if (G.OutEdges[v].Contains(v)) {
                        currentFVS.Add(v);
                        G.RemoveVertex(v);
                        localChanged = true;
                        continue;
                    }
                    
                    if (G.InEdges[v].Count == 0 || G.OutEdges[v].Count == 0) {
                        G.RemoveVertex(v);
                        localChanged = true;
                        continue;
                    }
                    
                    if (G.InEdges[v].Count == 1 || G.OutEdges[v].Count == 1) {
                        var in_edges = G.InEdges[v].ToList();
                        var out_edges = G.OutEdges[v].ToList();
                        G.RemoveVertex(v);
                        foreach (var u in in_edges) {
                            foreach (var w in out_edges) {
                                G.AddEdge(u, w);
                            }
                        }
                        localChanged = true;
                    }
                }
                if (localChanged) changed = true;
            }

            var sccs = FindSCCs(G);
            if (sccs.Count > 1) {

                for(int i = 0; i < sccs.Count; i++) {
                    foreach(var v in sccs[i]) sccMap[v] = i;

                    }

            }
        }

        foreach(var v in G.Vertices) {

                if (G.OutEdges[u].Contains(v)) {

                    visited.Add(u);
                    visited.Add(v);
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        return lb;

    static List<int> GreedyFVS(Graph G) {
        Graph g = G.Copy();
        List<int> fvs = new List<int>();
        while(g.Vertices.Count > 0) {

            while(changed) {
                changed = false;
                foreach(var v in g.Vertices.ToList()) {

                        changed = true;
                    } else if (g.InEdges[v].Count == 1 || g.OutEdges[v].Count == 1) {

                        var out_edges = g.OutEdges[v].ToList();
                        g.RemoveVertex(v);
                        foreach(var u in in_edges) foreach(var w in out_edges) g.AddEdge(u, w);
                        changed = true;
                    }
                }
            }
            if (g.Vertices.Count == 0) break;
            int max_deg = -1;
            int best_v = -1;
            foreach(var v in g.Vertices) {
                int deg = g.InEdges[v].Count + g.OutEdges[v].Count;
                if (deg > max_deg) { max_deg = deg; best_v = v; }
            }
            fvs.Add(best_v);
            g.RemoveVertex(best_v);
        }
        return fvs;

            if (branch_v != -1) break;
        }

        if (branch_v == -1) {
            int max_degree = -1;
            foreach(var v in G.Vertices) {
                int deg = G.InEdges[v].Count + G.OutEdges[v].Count;
                if (deg > max_degree) {
                    max_degree = deg;

                }

        G1.RemoveVertex(branch_v);
        var fvs1 = Solve(G1, current_best - fvs.Count - 1);
        
        if (fvs1 != null) {
            current_best = fvs.Count + 1 + fvs1.Count;
            best_local = new List<int>(fvs);

        if (fvs2 != null) {

        }

Given a universe of elements and a list of sets, choose set indices such that:
1) every element is covered, and
2) no element is covered more than once.

The evaluator is strict: only the exact expected solution is accepted.

**Input format (stdin)**
```
U S
e1 e2 e3 ...
e1 e2 ...
... (S lines total)
```
- `U` = number of elements in the universe (elements are `0..U-1`)
- `S` = number of available sets
- each following line is one set, listed as space-separated element IDs

**Output format (stdout)**
```
SOLUTION
i1 i2 i3 ... ik
```
or
```
NO SOLUTION
```

- `i1..ik` are 0-based set indices into the input list.

**What is checked**
1. Output format is valid.
2. Indices are valid and distinct.
3. Chosen indices are exactly the planted exact-cover solution.

Given a collection of sets, choose some of them so that every element in the universe appears in exactly one chosen set — no gaps and no overlaps. Think of tiling a floor with pre-cut pieces where every tile must be used exactly once and every square must be covered.

This is a classic NP-complete problem. Each test instance has exactly one valid solution, so grading is strict pass/fail. Subpasses increase the universe and set sizes.

View Python Code (1584 chars)
import sys

def main():
    lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    lines = [line.strip() for line in lines if line.strip()]
    if not lines:
        return
    
    U, S = map(int, lines[0].split())
    
    X = {i: set() for i in range(U)}
    Y = {}
    
    for i in range(S):
        parts = lines[i+1].split()
        elements = [int(p) for p in parts]
        Y[i] = elements
        for e in elements:
            if e in X:
                X[e].add(i)
                
    solution = []
    
    def select(X, Y, r):
        cols = []
        for j in Y[r]:
            for i in X[j]:
                for k in Y[i]:
                    if k != j:
                        X[k].remove(i)
            cols.append(X.pop(j))
        return cols

    def deselect(X, Y, r, cols):
        for j in reversed(Y[r]):
            X[j] = cols.pop()
            for i in X[j]:
                for k in Y[i]:
                    if k != j:
                        X[k].add(i)

    def solve():
        if not X:
            return True
        
        c = min(X, key=lambda k: len(X[k]))
        if len(X[c]) == 0:
            return False
            
        for r in sorted(list(X[c])):
            solution.append(r)
            cols = select(X, Y, r)
            if solve():
                return True
            deselect(X, Y, r, cols)
            solution.pop()
            
        return False
        
    if solve():
        print("SOLUTION")
        print(" ".join(map(str, sorted(solution))))
    else:
        print("NO SOLUTION")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

View Rust Code (3236 chars)
use std::io::{self, BufRead};

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut lines = stdin.lock().lines().filter_map(Result::ok);

    let first_line = match lines.next() {
        Some(l) => l,
        None => return,
    };
    let parts: Vec<usize> = first_line.split_whitespace().filter_map(|s| s.parse().ok()).collect();
    if parts.len() < 2 {
        return;
    }
    let n = parts[0];
    let m = parts[1];

    if n == 0 {
        println!("0\n");
        return;
    }

    let mut adj = vec![0u128; n];
    let mut edges_read = 0;
    while edges_read < m {
        if let Some(line) = lines.next() {
            let p: Vec<usize> = line.split_whitespace().filter_map(|s| s.parse().ok()).collect();
            if p.len() >= 2 {
                let u = p[0];
                let v = p[1];
                if u < n && v < n {
                    adj[u] |= 1 << v;
                    adj[v] |= 1 << u;
                }
                edges_read += 1;
            }
        } else {
            break;
        }
    }

    let mut best_cut = u32::MAX;
    let mut best_a = 0u128;

    fn solve(
        index: usize,
        a_count: usize,
        b_count: usize,
        current_cut: u32,
        assigned_a: u128,
        assigned_b: u128,
        best_cut: &mut u32,
        best_a: &mut u128,
        adj: &[u128],
        n: usize,
    ) {
        if current_cut >= *best_cut {
            return;
        }
        
        let mut lower_bound = current_cut;
        for i in index..n {
            let c_a = (adj[i] & assigned_b).count_ones();
            let c_b = (adj[i] & assigned_a).count_ones();
            lower_bound += c_a.min(c_b);
        }
        if lower_bound >= *best_cut {
            return;
        }

        if index == n {
            *best_cut = current_cut;
            *best_a = assigned_a;
            return;
        }

        let half = n / 2;

        let cost_a = (adj[index] & assigned_b).count_ones();
        let cost_b = (adj[index] & assigned_a).count_ones();

        let try_a = a_count < half;
        let try_b = b_count < half && index > 0; // Force node 0 to A to break symmetry

        if try_a && (!try_b || cost_a <= cost_b) {
            solve(index + 1, a_count + 1, b_count, current_cut + cost_a, assigned_a | (1 << index), assigned_b, best_cut, best_a, adj, n);
            if try_b {
                solve(index + 1, a_count, b_count + 1, current_cut + cost_b, assigned_a, assigned_b | (1 << index), best_cut, best_a, adj, n);
            }
        } else if try_b {
            solve(index + 1, a_count, b_count + 1, current_cut + cost_b, assigned_a, assigned_b | (1 << index), best_cut, best_a, adj, n);
            if try_a {
                solve(index + 1, a_count + 1, b_count, current_cut + cost_a, assigned_a | (1 << index), assigned_b, best_cut, best_a, adj, n);
            }
        }
    }

    solve(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, &mut best_cut, &mut best_a, &adj, n);

    let mut a_verts = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..n {
        if (best_a & (1 << i)) != 0 {
            a_verts.push(i);
        }
    }

    println!("{}", best_cut);
    let a_strs: Vec<String> = a_verts.iter().map(|v| v.to_string()).collect();
    println!("{}", a_strs.join(" "));
}

This is 0/1 Integer Linear Programming, a fundamental NP-hard optimisation problem. The test uses planted instances with a known unique optimum for strict pass/fail grading. Subpasses increase the number of variables and constraints.

Approach: The implementation provides a correct and efficient C++17 solution using a backtracking approach to solve the Maximum Weight Independent Set problem, which is equivalent to the requested 0/1 Integer Linear Program under the given constraints.

View C++ Code (2358 chars)
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>

/**
 * The problem is equivalent to the Maximum Weight Independent Set problem.
 * Given n variables and constraints (x_u + x_v <= 1), we can view this
 * as a graph where each constraint is an edge between u and v.
 * We want to select a subset of vertices such that no two are connected
 * by an edge, maximizing the sum of their weights.
 */

struct Solver {
    int n;
    std::vector<long long> weights;
    std::vector<std::vector<int>> adj;
    
    long long max_weight = -1;
    std::vector<int> best_assignment;
    std::vector<int> current_assignment;

    Solver(int n, std::vector<long long> weights, int m) : n(n), weights(weights) {
        adj.resize(n);
        current_assignment.assign(n, 0);
        best_assignment.assign(n, 0);
    }

    void add_constraint(int u, int v) {
        adj[u].push_back(v);
        adj[v].push_back(u);
    }

    bool is_safe(int v) {
        for (int neighbor : adj[v]) {
            if (current_assignment[neighbor] == 1) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }

    void solve(int idx, long long current_weight) {
        if (idx == n) {
            if (current_weight > max_weight) {
                max_weight = current_weight;
                best_assignment = current_assignment;
            }
            return;
        }

        // Try excluding variable idx
        current_assignment[idx] = 0;
        solve(idx + 1, current_weight);

        // Try including variable idx if safe
        if (is_safe(idx)) {
            current_assignment[idx] = 1;
            solve(idx + 1, current_weight + weights[idx]);
            current_assignment[idx] = 0; // backtrack
        }
    }
};

int main() {
    std::ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false);
    std::cin.tie(NULL);

    int n, m;
    if (!(std::cin >> n >> m)) return 0;

    std::vector<long long> c(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) std::cin >> c[i];

    Solver solver(n, c, m);
    for (int i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
        int u, v;
        std::cin >> u >> v;
        solver.add_constraint(u, v);
    }

    solver.solve(0, 0);

    std::cout << solver.max_weight << std::endl;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        std::cout << solver.best_assignment[i] << (i == n - 1 ? "" : " ");
    }
    std::cout << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

    std::vector<int> best_assignment;
    std::vector<int> current_assignment;

    Solver(int n, std::vector<long long> weights, int m) : n(n), weights(weights) {
        adj.resize(n);
        current_assignment.assign(n, 0);
        best_assignment.assign(n, 0);
    }

    void add_constraint(int u, int v) {
        adj[u].push_back(v);
        adj[v].push_back(u);
    }

    bool is_safe(int v) {
        for (int neighbor : adj[v]) {
            if (current_assignment[neighbor] == 1) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }

    void solve(int idx, long long current_weight) {
        if (idx == n) {
            if (current_weight > max_weight) {
                max_weight = current_weight;
                best_assignment = current_assignment;
            }
            return;
        }

        // Try excluding variable idx
        current_assignment[idx] = 0;
        solve(idx + 1, current_weight);

        // Try including variable idx if safe
        if (is_safe(idx)) {
            current_assignment[idx] = 1;
            solve(idx + 1, current_weight + weights[idx]);
            current_assignment[idx] = 0; // backtrack
        }
    }
};

int main() {
    std::ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false);
    std::cin.tie(NULL);

    int n, m;
    if (!(std::cin >> n >> m)) return 0;

    std::vector<long long> c(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) std::cin >> c[i];

    Solver solver(n, c, m);
    for (int i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
        int u, v;
        std::cin >> u >> v;
        solver.add_constraint(u, v);
    }

    solver.solve(0, 0);

    std::cout << solver.max_weight << std::endl;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        std::cout << solver.best_assignment[i] << (i == n - 1 ? "" : " ");
    }
    std::cout << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

layout(location = 0) in vec3 worldPos;

layout(location = 0) out vec4 outColor;

void main() {
    vec3 N = normalize(normal);
    vec3 L = normalize(ubo.lightPos.xyz - worldPos);
    vec3 V = normalize(ubo.cameraPos.xyz - worldPos);
    
    float NdotV = max(dot(N, V), 0.0);
    float rim = pow(1.0 - NdotV, 3.0);
    
    float diffuse = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
    
    vec3 baseColor = vec3(0.2, 0.3, 0.8);
    vec3 rimTint = vec3(1.0, 0.8, 0.5);
    
    vec3 finalColor = baseColor * (0.3 + 0.5 * diffuse) + rimTint * rim;
    outColor = vec4(finalColor, 1.0);
}

  mat4 model;

  mat4 projection;
  vec4 lightPos;

void main() {
    // Lambertian diffuse
    vec3 n = normalize(normal);
    vec3 l = normalize(ubo.lightPos.xyz - worldPos);
    float diffuse = max(dot(n, l), 0.0);
    float lighting = 0.4 + 0.6 * diffuse;

    // Brick pattern
    vec2 scale = vec2(8.0, 16.0);
    vec2 scaled_uv = uv * scale;

    // Staggered rows (half-brick offset every other row)
    float offset = step(0.5, fract(scaled_uv.y * 0.5)) * 0.5;
    vec2 offset_uv = vec2(scaled_uv.x + offset, scaled_uv.y);

    // Mortar mask
    vec2 fract_uv = fract(offset_uv);
    // mortar thickness is 0.05 in X and 0.1 in Y
    float x_mortar = step(fract_uv.x, 0.05);
    float y_mortar = step(fract_uv.y, 0.1);
    float is_mortar = max(x_mortar, y_mortar);

    // Colors
    vec3 brickColor = vec3(0.7, 0.2, 0.1);
    vec3 mortarColor = vec3(0.7, 0.7, 0.7);
    vec3 texColor = mix(brickColor, mortarColor, is_mortar);

    vec3 finalColor = texColor * lighting;
    outColor = vec4(finalColor, 1.0);
}

Typical Prompt:
You are writing a SPIR-V assembly geometry shader. It will be assembled with
spirv-as (Vulkan 1.0) and rendered using a fixed vertex shader and fragment shader.

**Geometry shader requirements:**
- `OpCapability Geometry`
- `OpMemoryModel Logical GLSL450`
- `OpEntryPoint Geometry %main "main"` listing ALL interface variables
- `OpExecutionMode %main ` (InputPoints/InputLines/Triangles/InputLinesAdjacency/InputTrianglesAdjacency)
- `OpExecutionMode %main ` (OutputPoints/OutputLineStrip/OutputTriangleStrip)
- `OpExecutionMode %main OutputVertices ` (max vertices emitted)
- `OpExecutionMode %main Invocations 1`

**Input from vertex shader (per-vertex arrays):**
The input gl_Position is in a gl_PerVertex block (must be decorated with Block + BuiltIn Position).
```
%gl_PerVertex_in = OpTypeStruct %v4float
OpDecorate %gl_PerVertex_in Block
OpMemberDecorate %gl_PerVertex_in 0 BuiltIn Position
; Array size depends on input primitive:
; InputPoints: 1, InputLines: 2, Triangles: 3
; InputLinesAdjacency: 4, InputTrianglesAdjacency: 6
%arr_pv_in = OpTypeArray %gl_PerVertex_in %uint_N
%ptr_in_arr_pv = OpTypePointer Input %arr_pv_in
%gl_in = OpVariable %ptr_in_arr_pv Input
; Access: OpAccessChain %ptr_in_v4 %gl_in %int_i %int_0 -> gl_in[i].gl_Position
```

User-defined inputs are also arrays of the same size:
```
layout(location = 0) in vec3 worldPos[]; ; positions in clip space
layout(location = 1) in vec3 normal[]; ; vertex normals
layout(location = 2) in vec3 color[]; ; per-vertex colors
```

**Output (per emitted vertex):**
The output gl_Position is in a gl_PerVertex block:
```
%gl_PerVertex_out = OpTypeStruct %v4float
OpDecorate %gl_PerVertex_out Block
OpMemberDecorate %gl_PerVertex_out 0 BuiltIn Position
%ptr_out_pv = OpTypePointer Output %gl_PerVertex_out
%gl_out = OpVariable %ptr_out_pv Output
; Store: OpAccessChain %ptr_out_v4 %gl_out %int_0 -> gl_out.gl_Position
```
```
layout(location = 0) out vec3 outColor; ; color for fragment shader
```

**Emit vertices with:** `OpEmitVertex` after storing gl_Position and outColor.
**End primitive with:** `OpEndPrimitive` after emitting a complete strip.

**Available UBO (set=0, binding=0) - accessible from geometry shader:**
Same layout as test 41 (model/view/proj matrices, lightPos, cameraPos, params).

**Write ONLY the complete SPIR-V assembly text for the geometry shader.**


**Input primitive:** InputPoints (1 vertex per invocation, array size 1)
**Geometry:** 25 colored points in a 5x5 grid spread across [-0.8, 0.8].

**Task:** Expand each point into a small colored quad (4 vertices as triangle strip).
1. Read gl_in[0].gl_Position (the point position).
2. Read color[0] (the point's color).
3. Define a half-size: h = 0.04.
4. Emit 4 vertices forming a quad centered on the point:
- (x-h, y-h), (x+h, y-h), (x-h, y+h), (x+h, y+h)
- All with z=0, w=1, and the same color.
5. Output as triangle strip, max 4 vertices.

layout(lines) in;
layout(triangle_strip, max_vertices = 7) out;

layout(location = 0) in vec3 in_worldPos[];
layout(location = 1) in vec3 in_normal[];
layout(location = 2) in vec3 in_color[];

layout(location = 0) out vec3 outColor;

void main() {
    vec4 p0 = gl_in[0].gl_Position;
    vec4 p1 = gl_in[1].gl_Position;
    vec3 c0 = in_color[0];
    vec3 c1 = in_color[1];

    vec2 dir = p1.xy - p0.xy;
    vec2 perp = normalize(vec2(-dir.y, dir.x));

    vec2 mid = p0.xy + 0.75 * dir;

    vec2 p0_p = p0.xy + perp * 0.015;
    vec2 p0_m = p0.xy - perp * 0.015;
    vec2 mid_p = mid + perp * 0.015;
    vec2 mid_m = mid - perp * 0.015;

    // Shaft
    outColor = c0;
    gl_Position = vec4(p0_p, p0.z, p0.w); EmitVertex();
    gl_Position = vec4(p0_m, p0.z, p0.w); EmitVertex();
    gl_Position = vec4(mid_p, p0.z, p0.w); EmitVertex();
    gl_Position = vec4(mid_m, p0.z, p0.w); EmitVertex();
    EndPrimitive();

    // Arrowhead
    vec2 tip_p = mid + perp * 0.05;
    vec2 tip_m = mid - perp * 0.05;
    outColor = c1;
    gl_Position = vec4(tip_p, p1.z, p1.w); EmitVertex();
    gl_Position = vec4(tip_m, p1.z, p1.w); EmitVertex();
    gl_Position = vec4(p1.xy, p1.z, p1.w); EmitVertex();
    EndPrimitive();
}

    vec4 p0 = gl_in[i].gl_Position;

- OpCapability (17): word_count=2, operand=capability (1=Shader)
- OpExtInstImport (11): result_id, name_string
- OpMemoryModel (14): word_count=3, addressing=0(Logical), model=1(GLSL450)
- OpEntryPoint (15): execution_model=4(Fragment), entry_id, name, interface_vars...
- OpExecutionMode (16): entry_id, mode=7(OriginUpperLeft)
- OpDecorate (71): target, decoration, operands
- OpTypeVoid (19), OpTypeFunction (33), OpTypeFloat (22), OpTypeVector (23)
- OpTypePointer (32), OpVariable (59), OpConstant (43)
- OpFunction (54), OpFunctionEnd (56), OpLabel (248)
- OpLoad (61), OpStore (62), OpReturn (253)
- OpCompositeConstruct (80), OpCompositeExtract (81)
- OpDot (148), OpFMul (133), OpFAdd (129), OpFSub (131), OpFNegate (127)
- OpExtInst (12): GLSL.std.450 ext instructions

**Decoration values:** Location=30, DescriptorSet=34, Binding=33, Block=2, Offset=35

**Available inputs (from vertex shader):**
```
location 0: vec3 worldPos
location 1: vec3 normal
location 2: vec2 uv
location 3: vec3 tangent
location 4: vec3 color
```

**UBO (set=0, binding=0):** mat4 model(0), mat4 view(64), mat4 projection(128),
vec4 lightPos(192), vec4 cameraPos(208), vec4 params(224).

**Required output:** location 0: vec4 outColor

**GLSL Compute Shader Interface:**

```
#version 450

layout(local_size_x = 256) in;

// Each body is stored as two consecutive vec4s:
// vec4(position.xyz, mass)
// vec4(velocity.xyz, 0.0)
// So body i starts at index i*2 in the buffer.

layout(set = 0, binding = 0) readonly buffer InputBodies {
vec4 inData[]; // length = N * 2
};

layout(set = 0, binding = 1) buffer OutputBodies {
vec4 outData[]; // length = N * 2
};

layout(set = 0, binding = 2) uniform Params {
uvec4 counts; // counts.x = N (number of bodies)
vec4 physics; // physics.x = dt, physics.y = softening, physics.z = G
};
```

**Task:** Write a compute shader that performs ONE timestep of gravitational
N-body simulation using the leapfrog/Euler integration method. Each invocation
handles one body (gl_GlobalInvocationID.x), reading its position and velocity
from inData and writing updated values to outData. The acceleration should be
computed from all other bodies using:

acc += G * mass_j * (pos_j - pos_i) / (|pos_j - pos_i|^2 + softening^2)^(3/2)

Velocity is advanced by acc * dt and position is advanced by vel * dt. The
shader will be dispatched ceil(N/256) workgroups in X and run multiple times
with ping-pong buffers for the required number of timesteps.

**Critical Requirements:**
- Guard against gl_GlobalInvocationID.x >= N
- Use the softening parameter to avoid singularities
- Skip self-interaction (i == j)
- Write BOTH position+mass and velocity vec4s to output

Test 47: Hash Mining / Proof of Work (WGSL Compute) Score: 4.00 / 5
Typical Prompt:
Write a WGSL compute shader for hash mining (proof-of-work).

**WGSL Compute Shader Interface:**

```wgsl
@group(0) @binding(0) var baseData : array;
@group(0) @binding(1) var result : array;
@group(0) @binding(2) var params : vec4;
// params.x = difficulty, params.y = range_start, params.z = range_size

@compute @workgroup_size(256)
fn main(@builtin(global_invocation_id) gid : vec3) { ... }
```

**Task:** Write a compute shader that searches for a uint32 nonce such that
the custom hash of (baseData XOR nonce) has at least `difficulty` trailing
zero bits in the 64-bit output.

**Hash function (MUST match exactly):**
```
function custom_hash(data[16], nonce) -> (h0, h1):
state[0..15] = data[0..15]
for i in 0..15: state[i] ^= (nonce + i)

// 8 rounds of quarter-round mixing (ChaCha-like)
repeat 8 times:
for each group of 4 consecutive elements (i, i+1, i+2, i+3):
a += b; d ^= a; d = rotl(d, 16)
c += d; b ^= c; b = rotl(b, 12)
a += b; d ^= a; d = rotl(d, 8)
c += d; b ^= c; b = rotl(b, 7)

// Fold 16 words to 2:
h0 = state[0] ^ state[2] ^ state[4] ^ state[6] ^ state[8] ^ state[10] ^ state[12] ^ state[14]
h1 = state[1] ^ state[3] ^ state[5] ^ state[7] ^ state[9] ^ state[11] ^ state[13] ^ state[15]
return (h0, h1) // h0 is low 32 bits
```

**Trailing zero count:** Count trailing zero bits of the 64-bit value [h0 | (h1 << 32)].
That is, count from h0's LSB first; if h0 == 0, add 32 and continue counting from h1.

**Algorithm:**
1. Each thread computes: my_nonce = params.y + gid.x (range_start + thread ID)
2. Guard: if gid.x >= params.z, return (out of range)
3. Compute hash, count trailing zeros
4. If trailing_zeros >= difficulty:
Write result[0]=1u, result[1]=nonce, result[2]=h0, result[3]=h1
(Race writes are acceptable - any valid nonce will be verified on CPU)

**Important WGSL notes:**
- Use `var state : array` for the mutable hash state.
- WGSL rotation: `(x << shift) | (x >> (32u - shift))` — all values must be u32.
- The inner quarter-round loop MUST be unrolled (write out all 4 groups
of state[0..3], state[4..7], state[8..11], state[12..15] explicitly).
- Do NOT use atomics. Plain stores to result[] are sufficient.
- All integer literals must be typed: use `0u`, `1u`, `16u`, `32u` etc.

The shader will be dispatched with ceil(range_size / 256) workgroups.
Only ONE dispatch is performed - find the nonce in a single pass.

Subpass 2: difficulty=12 bits, search_range=16,777,216
Subpass 3: difficulty=16 bits, search_range=268,435,456

Test 48: 2D Fluid Simulation - Lattice Boltzmann (SPIR-V ASM Compute) Score: 0.00 / 5
Typical Prompt:
Write a SPIR-V assembly compute shader for 2D Lattice Boltzmann fluid simulation.

**SPIR-V Assembly Compute Shader Interface:**

The shader uses the D2Q9 Lattice Boltzmann model for 2D fluid simulation.

**D2Q9 velocity directions (index k -> (cx, cy)):**
```
k=0: ( 0, 0) w=4/9 (rest)
k=1: ( 1, 0) w=1/9 (east)
k=2: ( 0, 1) w=1/9 (north)
k=3: (-1, 0) w=1/9 (west)
k=4: ( 0,-1) w=1/9 (south)
k=5: ( 1, 1) w=1/36 (NE)
k=6: (-1, 1) w=1/36 (NW)
k=7: (-1,-1) w=1/36 (SW)
k=8: ( 1,-1) w=1/36 (SE)
```

**Buffer layout:**
- Binding 0 (storage, read-only): float array, length W*H*9
Index = (y * W + x) * 9 + k
- Binding 1 (storage, read-write): float array, length W*H*9 (output, NOT writeonly)
- Binding 2 (uniform): { uvec4(W, H, 0, 0), vec4(omega, 0, 0, 0) }

**Algorithm (per cell at gl_GlobalInvocationID.xy):**
Compute one LBM step (collision + streaming) for each lattice cell. Guard against
out-of-bounds (x >= W or y >= H). For the cell distributions f[0..8], compute
macroscopic density rho and velocity (ux, uy) using the D2Q9 directions. Apply
the BGK collision update with:

cu = cx[k]*ux + cy[k]*uy
feq = w[k] * rho * (1 + 3*cu + 4.5*cu*cu - 1.5*(ux*ux + uy*uy))
f_out = f[k] + omega * (feq - f[k])

Then stream each f_out to the neighbor cell (x+cx[k], y+cy[k]) with periodic
wraparound in both axes. Write to the output buffer at the corresponding
neighbor index for k.

**SPIR-V requirements:**
- OpCapability Shader
- OpExecutionMode with LocalSize 16 16 1
- Use gl_GlobalInvocationID for (x, y)
- Declare runtime arrays for storage buffers with OpDecorate ArrayStride 4
- Use OpSMod or manual modulo for periodic boundary conditions

Test 49: Parallel Prefix Sum (SPIR-V Binary Compute) Score: 0.00 / 5
Typical Prompt:
Write a SPIR-V binary compute shader (hex-encoded) for parallel inclusive prefix sum.

**SPIR-V Binary (hex-encoded) Compute Shader Interface:**

You must produce raw SPIR-V binary encoded as a hex string (no spaces, no 0x prefix).
The binary must start with the SPIR-V magic number 0x07230203.

**Required layout:**
```
Binding 0 (set=0): Storage buffer (read-only) - uint array, length N
Binding 1 (set=0): Storage buffer (read-write) - uint array, length N
Binding 2 (set=0): Uniform buffer - uint4: [N, 0, 0, 0]

Local size: 256 x 1 x 1
```

**Algorithm:** Inclusive prefix sum (scan)
- Input: [a0, a1, a2, a3, ...]
- Output: [a0, a0+a1, a0+a1+a2, a0+a1+a2+a3, ...]

Compute an inclusive scan over the input array. For N <= 256, use a shared-memory
scan within a single workgroup (synchronize as needed). For N > 256, a naive
fallback (each thread sums all previous elements) is acceptable but slow; full
marks require a multi-workgroup scan.

**SPIR-V binary encoding notes:**
- Little-endian uint32 words
- Magic: 0x07230203
- Version: 0x00010000 (1.0)
- Bound: upper bound on all IDs used + 1
- Schema: 0
- OpCapability Shader = [0x00020011, 0x00000001]
- OpMemoryModel Logical GLSL450 = [0x00030006, 0x00000001, 0x00000001]
- OpEntryPoint GLCompute = opcode 0x0000000F, execution model 5
- OpExecutionMode LocalSize = opcode 0x00000010, mode 17 (LocalSize)
- OpDecorate Binding = decoration 33
- OpDecorate DescriptorSet = decoration 34
- OpDecorate ArrayStride = decoration 6
- OpDecorate BufferBlock or Block = decoration 2 or 3
- OpTypeInt 32 0 = unsigned int
- OpTypePointer StorageBuffer = storage class 12
- OpVariable StorageBuffer = storage class 12

Encode every uint32 word as exactly 8 hex characters (little-endian).

```glsl
vec4 weights; // weights.x=sepWeight, weights.y=alignWeight, weights.z=cohWeight, weights.w=maxSpeed
vec4 bounds; // bounds.x=boundSize, bounds.y=boundForce
};
```

**Task:** Write a compute shader that performs ONE timestep of 3D boid
flocking simulation (Reynolds' rules). Each invocation handles one boid
(gl_GlobalInvocationID.x), reading its position/velocity from inData and
writing updated values to outData. Use separation/align/cohesion with the
provided radii and weights, average neighbor contributions, and apply the
boundary force when a component exceeds boundSize*0.4 (push toward center
using boundForce and boundSize*0.5 scaling). Update velocity by accel*dt,
clamp speed to maxSpeed, then update position by vel*dt.

**Critical Requirements:**
- Guard against gl_GlobalInvocationID.x >= N
- Skip self (i == j) and zero-distance neighbors
- Average the accumulated forces by neighbor count (avoid division by zero)
- Clamp velocity magnitude to maxSpeed


**Flocking Parameters (constant across all subpasses):**
Separation radius: 2.0, weight: 1.5
Alignment radius: 5.0, weight: 1.0
Cohesion radius: 8.0, weight: 1.0
Max speed: 5.0
Bound size: 50.0, bound force: 0.5

**Test Configurations:**
Subpass 0: N=128, timesteps=50, dt=0.05
Subpass 1: N=256, timesteps=100, dt=0.05

Subpass 3: N=1024, timesteps=200, dt=0.05
Subpass 4: N=2048, timesteps=200, dt=0.05
Subpass 5: N=4096, timesteps=200, dt=0.05

Write the complete GLSL compute shader source code.
The shader performs ONE step. It will be dispatched multiple times with
ping-pong buffers for the required number of timesteps.

- Most sensors come in triples (3 redundant units). Any can fail silently!
- `*_valid` flags exist but may be WRONG (sensor can fail without flagging)

- `dt` is the timestep (~0.05s = 20 Hz)

**Output:** Return a dict with these control keys:
```
elevator: -1.0 (nose down) to +1.0 (nose up), RELATIVE TO TRIM
(0.0 = maintain current trimmed attitude)
aileron: -1.0 (roll left) to +1.0 (roll right)
rudder: -1.0 (yaw left) to +1.0 (yaw right)
throttle_1: 0.0 (idle) to 1.0 (full thrust) — left engine
throttle_2: 0.0 (idle) to 1.0 (full thrust) — right engine
elevator_trim: -1.0 to +1.0 (adjusts the trim baseline over time)
flaps: 0 to 40 (degrees)
speedbrake: 0.0 to 1.0
gear: 0 (up) or 1 (down)
```
NOTE: If you omit a key, the current value is maintained. Throttle defaults
to the current setting if not specified.

**Critical Design Requirements:**
1. **Sensor fusion**: Cross-check redundant sensors, and cross-check other physical
properties. If GPS altitude is dropping, radar altitude is stable, and barometric
altitude is climbing - two failures have occured, and you have to pick wisely.
2. **Aerodynamic simulation**: The flight model includes a full aerodynamic model, so
brush up on your knowledge of stalls, asymetric thurst, yaw dampening, and trim.
5. Vne is (~365 KIAS / Mach 0.82).
6. **Persistence**: You may define module-level variables for PID integral terms,
previous values, etc. They persist across calls within a scenario.

Your single autopilot function must handle every scenario, including over a dozen
historical aviation accidents. The same code is tested against every scenario.

**Traction/Surface** (3 keys):

Key facts:
- Wheel speed sensors (4): FL, FR, RL, RR in km/h. Any can fail.
- Gyroscopes (3): yaw rate in degrees/second. Any can fail silently.
- Accelerometers (3): longitudinal and lateral in m/s². Any can fail.
- GPS (2): position in meters, speed in km/h. Can lose signal.
- Lidar (12 beams): range in meters at angles from -90° to +90°.
- Vision (3 independent systems): lane line distances, types (solid/dashed),
obstacle detection (bool + distance + relative speed), speed limit signs,
lane offset, road curvature. ANY can fail or flicker!
- `estimated_mu`: estimated tire-road friction (1.0=dry, <0.3=ice).
- `target_speed_kmh`: desired speed. `target_lane`: desired lane (0-2).
- `*_valid` flags exist but may be WRONG on failed sensors.
- Sensors can FLICKER: randomly return invalid data for a few frames.

**Output:** Return a dict:
```
steering: -1.0 (full left) to +1.0 (full right)
0.0 = straight ahead
throttle: 0.0 (no power) to 1.0 (full power)
brake: 0.0 (no brake) to 1.0 (emergency stop)
```
If you omit a key, the current value is maintained.

**Critical Design Requirements:**
1. **Sensor fusion**: Cross-check redundant sensors. Median/voting for disagreements.
2. **Lane keeping**: Stay centered in lane using vision line distances and lidar.
3. **Speed control**: Maintain target speed, respect speed limits.
4. **Obstacle avoidance**: If obstacle detected, brake and/or lane change.
5. **Traction management**: On low-mu surfaces, reduce speed, gentler inputs.
6. **Graceful degradation**: Handle sensor failures, flickering data.
7. **Persistence**: Module-level variables persist across calls for filtering/PID.

**Test Scenarios (25 total):**
0. Normal highway cruise
1. Gentle curve
2. Slow vehicle ahead
3. Emergency stop — stopped vehicle
4. Cut-in from adjacent lane
5. Ice patch — reduced traction
6. Aquaplaning — very low friction
7. Wheel speed sensor failure (FL)
8. Two wheel speed sensors fail
9. Gyro sensor failure
10. GPS signal lost
11. Vision system 1 failure
12. All vision systems flickering
13. Front lidar beams fail
14. Steering angle sensors disagree
15. Total brake failure
16. Throttle stuck at 30%
17. Road debris
18. Dense traffic
19. Crosswind gust
20. Steering partially jammed
21. Ice + stopped vehicle
22. Flickering sensors in curve
23. Reduced visibility
24. Multi-failure + obstacle

Your single autopilot function must handle ALL scenarios.

Test 53: Spacecraft Orbital Docking Autopilot (Python) Score: 24.90 / 25
Typical Prompt:
Write a Python autopilot to dock a spacecraft with a space station in orbit.

**CRITICAL ORBITAL MECHANICS INSIGHT:**
In orbit, relative motion is COUNTER-INTUITIVE:
- Thrusting TOWARD the target (prograde if behind) raises your orbit → you SLOW DOWN relative to target
- To catch up: thrust RETROGRADE (backward!) to lower orbit → you go FASTER
- Radial thrusts cause oscillation, not direct movement
- Cross-track corrections require thrusts at specific orbital positions
- Near the target (<50m), approximate as linear (CW equations work)
- Far away (>200m), full orbital mechanics dominate

**Function Signature:**
```python
def autopilot_step(state: dict, dt: float) -> dict:
```

**Input:** `state` is a dict with 110 keys:

Key sensor notes:
- Relative position/velocity in LVLH frame: x=radial (up), y=along-track (velocity dir), z=cross-track
- NEGATIVE y = behind station (most common start). Must CLOSE the y gap.
- Range finders give scalar distance. Radar/lidar give 3D relative pos/vel.
- All sensors can fail silently! Cross-check redundant sensors.
- Docking camera only active within 500m. Gives bearing to docking port.
- Ground station data updates every ~30s (stale but reliable).

**Output:** Return a dict:
```
thrust_x: -1.0 to +1.0 (radial: + = away from Earth)
thrust_y: -1.0 to +1.0 (along-track: + = prograde)
thrust_z: -1.0 to +1.0 (cross-track: + = north)
att_rate_roll: rad/s (max ±0.035)
att_rate_pitch: rad/s (max ±0.035)
att_rate_yaw: rad/s (max ±0.035)
```
Each thrust axis: 220N per thruster, Isp=290s. Fuel is LIMITED (~500 kg).

**Docking Success Criteria:**
- Range < 2m AND relative speed < 0.3 m/s

**Approach Strategy Hints:**
1. Far (>200m): Use Hohmann-like transfer — retrograde to lower orbit if behind
2. Medium (50-200m): Gentle corrections, V-bar approach preferred
3. Close (<50m): Linear regime, direct thrust corrections OK
4. Final (<10m): Very gentle, < 0.1 m/s approach speed

**Test Scenarios (25 total):**
0. V-bar approach — 200m behind
1. V-bar approach — 500m behind
2. V-bar close approach — 50m
3. R-bar approach — 200m below
4. Approach from above — 200m

19. Flickering range + radar sensors
20. Low fuel — only 50 kg remaining
21. Cross-track + radar failure
22. Higher orbit — 450km
23. All range sensors very noisy
24. Multi-failure + uncommanded thrust + offset

Your single autopilot function must handle ALL scenarios.

**ILS Approach Key Concepts:**
- `glideslope_N_dots`: deviation from 3° glideslope (+above/-below), 3 receivers
- `localizer_N_dots`: deviation from runway centerline (+right/-left), 3 receivers
- `radio_alt_ft`: height above ground (critical for flare)
- `dme_N_nm`: distance to runway threshold
- `weight_on_wheels`: True when landed
- `target_vref_kt`: reference approach speed (typically 137kt)
- `decision_height_ft`: minimum altitude to continue approach (200ft CAT I)
- Elevator command 0 = trimmed flight. Positive = pitch up.

**Output:** Return a dict with any of:
```
elevator: -1.0 (nose down) to +1.0 (nose up), relative to trim
aileron: -1.0 (roll left) to +1.0 (roll right)
rudder: -1.0 (yaw left) to +1.0 (yaw right)
throttle_1: 0.0 to 1.0 (left engine)
throttle_2: 0.0 to 1.0 (right engine)
elevator_trim: -1.0 to +1.0
flaps: degrees (0-40)
gear: 0.0 (up) or 1.0 (down)
speedbrake: 0.0 (retracted) to 1.0 (full)
spoiler: 0.0 or 1.0 (ground spoilers, deploy after touchdown)
autobrake: 0.0 to 1.0 (braking force after touchdown)
reverse_1: 0.0 to 1.0 (left engine reverse thrust)
reverse_2: 0.0 to 1.0 (right engine reverse thrust)
```

**Approach Phases:**
1. **Intercept** (>1000ft): Track glideslope and localizer, configure for landing
2. **Approach** (1000ft-200ft): Stabilise on glideslope, speed, config
3. **Flare** (<50ft radio alt): Reduce descent rate, idle thrust
4. **Touchdown & Rollout**: Deploy spoilers, reverse thrust, autobrake

**Go-Around:**
If the approach is unstable or unsafe, abort the landing:
- Apply TOGA thrust (throttle 1.0), pitch up, retract speedbrake
- Climb to 1500ft AGL — this completes the go-around
- The sim will then **restart** from a stable approach position with the
**same failures and weather**. Your autopilot must land on the retry.
- Each go-around costs a **0.1 point penalty** on a perfect landing.
- After **10 go-arounds** the scenario fails (score 0.0).

**Scoring:**
- **1.0** — Normal landing: stopped on the runway, or slowed below 50kt
with >30% runway remaining (pilot takes over to taxi).
Minus 0.1 per go-around.
- **0.5** — Hard landing: touchdown vertical speed 360–600 fpm.
Aircraft needs inspection but is reusable, everyone walks away.
- **0.1** — Minor overrun: aircraft rolls off the end but is caught by the
EMAS arrestor bed (within 150m past runway end). Everyone safe,
aircraft damaged.
- **0.0** — Catastrophic: touchdown >600 fpm, major overrun
beyond EMAS, runway excursion, CFIT, or failure to land. Write-off or
loss of life.

**Test Scenarios (25 total):**
0. Normal ILS approach CAT I
1. Short final — 3nm
2. High on glideslope
3. Low on glideslope
4. Offset from centerline
5. Single engine failure on final [Kegworth (1989) / BA 38 (2008)]
6. Windshear on short final [Delta 191 (1985)]
7. Strong crosswind — 25kt
8. Gusty crosswind — 15kt gusting 30
9. CAT III low visibility
10. Slippery wet runway [Overruns at LGA, MDW]
11. Icy runway
12. Glideslope receiver 1+2 failed
13. Localizer 1 stuck + 2 biased
14. All radar altimeters failed
15. Elevator partially jammed
16. Aileron stuck 5° left
17. Unstabilised — too fast
18. Heavy weight landing
19. Asymmetric flap extension
20. Dual engine failure — glide approach [Gimli Glider (1983) / US Airways 1549 (2009)]
21. Missed approach required
22. Severe turbulence on final
23. ILS signal flickering
24. Engine failure + crosswind + wet runway [Multiple incidents]

Your single autopilot function must handle ALL scenarios.
Persistence: module-level variables persist across calls within a scenario,
but are **reset** between scenarios and between go-around attempts.

Test 55: Can your write a chess bot? (C++) Score: 0.00 / 40
Typical Prompt:
Write a C++ chess bot that for any given chess position, returns the best move to make (or the best
move you can find before the timeout).

You receive the chess position as a string in FEN notation, and you must return the move in
disambiguated algebraic notation (including the starting square, piece type, and destination square).

See:
- https://www.chess.com/terms/fen-chess

Here is an example FEN representing the starting position with white to move:
```
rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1
```

Here is an example disambiguated algebraic move:
```
pe2e4
```
This represents the king's pawn opening - moving the pawn from e2 to e4.

**Move notation rules:**
- Piece letter (lowercase p for pawn, uppercase N/B/R/Q/K for others) + source square + destination square.
- Use "x" between source and destination for captures: `pe4xd5`
- Promotion: append `/` and the piece letter, e.g. `pe7e8/Q`
- Castling: `O-O` (kingside) or `O-O-O` (queenside).
- En passant: append `ep`, e.g. `pe5xd6ep`
- Check: append `+`, e.g. `Bb4c5+`
- Checkmate: append `#`, e.g. `Qd1h5#`

**Input format (stdin, two lines):**
```
timeout_in_seconds
fen_string
```

**Output format (stdout, one line):**
```
move_in_disambiguated_algebraic
```

timeout_in_seconds will be at least 5. Your code will be compiled with full optimisations and
run on a machine with multiple cores, so threading is encouraged.

**Environment:**
Platform: Windows 11 (build 10.0.26200)
Architecture: AMD64
CPU: AMD64 Family 23 Model 8 Stepping 2, AuthenticAMD
Core count: 64
Memory: 127.87 GB
SIMD: AVX, AVX2, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, SSSE3
SIMD detail: AVX=yes, AVX-512F=no, AVX2=yes, SSE=yes, SSE2=yes, SSE3=yes, SSE4.1=yes, SSE4.2=yes, SSSE3=yes

**C++ Compiler:**
MSVC cl 19.50.35730 | std=c++20 (/std:c++20)

Be sure that any deviation from the C++ standard library is supported by the given compiler,
as referencing the wrong intrinsics or non-standard header (like 'bits/stdc++.h') could fail your submission.

const fs = require('fs');

function distance(p1, p2) {
    const dx = p1.x - p2.x;
    const dy = p1.y - p2.y;
    return Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
}

function solve() {
    const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
    const data = JSON.parse(input);
    const depot = { x: data.depot[0], y: data.depot[1] };
    const maxTrucks = data.truckCount;
    const packages = data.packages;

    if (!packages || packages.length === 0) {
        console.log(JSON.stringify({ routes: [] }));
        return;
    }

    packages.forEach(p => {
        p.angle = Math.atan2(p.y - depot.y, p.x - depot.x);
    });

    packages.sort((a, b) => a.angle - b.angle);

    const routes = [];
    const numRoutes = Math.min(maxTrucks, packages.length);
    const chunkSize = Math.ceil(packages.length / numRoutes);

    for (let i = 0; i < numRoutes; i++) {
        const chunk = packages.slice(i * chunkSize, (i + 1) * chunkSize);
        if (chunk.length === 0) break;

        let unvisited = [...chunk];
        let curr = depot;
        const route = [];

        while (unvisited.length > 0) {
            let bestDist = Infinity;
            let bestIdx = -1;
            for (let j = 0; j < unvisited.length; j++) {
                const dist = distance(curr, unvisited[j]);
                if (dist < bestDist) {
                    bestDist = dist;
                    bestIdx = j;
                }
            }
            curr = unvisited[bestIdx];
            route.push(curr);
            unvisited.splice(bestIdx, 1);
        }

        let improved = true;
        let iter = 0;
        while (improved && iter < 100) {
            improved = false;
            iter++;
            for (let j = 0; j < route.length; j++) {
                for (let k = j + 1; k < route.length; k++) {
                    const p1 = j === 0 ? depot : route[j - 1];
                    const p2 = route[j];
                    const p3 = route[k];
                    const p4 = k === route.length - 1 ? depot : route[k + 1];

                    const dOld = distance(p1, p2) + distance(p3, p4);
                    const dNew = distance(p1, p3) + distance(p2, p4);

                    if (dNew < dOld - 1e-6) {
                        let left = j;
                        let right = k;
                        while (left < right) {
                            const temp = route[left];
                            route[left] = route[right];
                            route[right] = temp;
                            left++;
                            right--;
                        }
                        improved = true;
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        routes.push(route.map(p => p.id));
    }

    console.log(JSON.stringify({ routes }));
}

solve();

const fs = require('fs');
const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
const data = JSON.parse(input);

const { width, height, grid, ignitions, towns, cutBudget } = data;

const gridArr = grid.map(row => row.split(''));

towns.sort((a, b) => b.value - a.value);

let remainingBudget = cutBudget;
let firebreaks = [];

const isIgnition = (x, y) => {
    return ignitions.some(ig => ig[0] === x && ig[1] === y);
};

for (const town of towns) {
    if (remainingBudget === 0) break;
    
    const neighbors = [
        [town.x, town.y - 1],
        [town.x, town.y + 1],
        [town.x - 1, town.y],
        [town.x + 1, town.y]
    ];
    
    let neededCuts = [];
    let possibleToProtect = true;
    
    for (const [nx, ny] of neighbors) {
        if (nx >= 0 && nx < width && ny >= 0 && ny < height) {
            if (gridArr[ny][nx] === '.') {
                if (isIgnition(nx, ny)) {
                    possibleToProtect = false;
                    break;
                }
                neededCuts.push([nx, ny]);
            }
        }
    }
    
    if (possibleToProtect && neededCuts.length <= remainingBudget) {
        for (const [nx, ny] of neededCuts) {
            firebreaks.push([nx, ny]);
            gridArr[ny][nx] = '~'; // mark as cut
        }
        remainingBudget -= neededCuts.length;
    }
}

const fs = require('fs');

function solve() {
    const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
    if (!input.trim()) return;
    const data = JSON.parse(input);
    const grid = data.grid;
    const robots = data.robots;
    const jobs = data.jobs;

    const H = grid.length;
    const W = grid[0].length;

    let maxRobotId = -1;
    for (const r of robots) {
        if (r.id > maxRobotId) maxRobotId = r.id;
    }
    const assignments = [];
    for (let i = 0; i <= maxRobotId; i++) {
        assignments.push([]);
    }

    const points = [];
    for (const r of robots) points.push({x: r.x, y: r.y});
    for (const j of jobs) points.push({x: j.x, y: j.y});

    const pointIdx = new Map();
    const uniquePoints = [];
    for (const p of points) {
        const key = p.y * W + p.x;
        if (!pointIdx.has(key)) {
            pointIdx.set(key, uniquePoints.length);
            uniquePoints.push(p);
        }
    }

    const numPoints = uniquePoints.length;
    const dists = Array(numPoints);
    const dx = [0, 1, 0, -1];
    const dy = [1, 0, -1, 0];

    const q = new Int32Array(H * W * 2);
    const d = new Int32Array(H * W);

    for (let i = 0; i < numPoints; i++) {
        const start = uniquePoints[i];
        let head = 0, tail = 0;
        q[tail++] = start.x;
        q[tail++] = start.y;
        
        d.fill(1e9);
        d[start.y * W + start.x] = 0;
        
        while (head < tail) {
            const cx = q[head++];
            const cy = q[head++];
            const curD = d[cy * W + cx];
            
            for (let dir = 0; dir < 4; dir++) {
                const nx = cx + dx[dir];
                const ny = cy + dy[dir];
                if (nx >= 0 && nx < W && ny >= 0 && ny < H) {
                    if (grid[ny].charCodeAt(nx) !== 35) { // 35 is '#'
                        const nIdx = ny * W + nx;
                        if (d[nIdx] > curD + 1) {
                            d[nIdx] = curD + 1;
                            q[tail++] = nx;
                            q[tail++] = ny;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        
        dists[i] = new Int32Array(numPoints);
        for (let j = 0; j < numPoints; j++) {
            const p = uniquePoints[j];
            dists[i][j] = d[p.y * W + p.x];
        }
    }

    function getDist(x1, y1, x2, y2) {
        const k1 = pointIdx.get(y1 * W + x1);
        const k2 = pointIdx.get(y2 * W + x2);
        return dists[k1][k2];
    }

    const unassigned = new Set(jobs);
    const robotPos = new Map();
    for (const r of robots) {
        robotPos.set(r.id, { x: r.x, y: r.y });
    }

    while (unassigned.size > 0) {
        let bestPair = null;
        for (const job of unassigned) {
            for (const r of robots) {
                const pos = robotPos.get(r.id);
                const dist = getDist(pos.x, pos.y, job.x, job.y);
                if (dist > 1e8) continue; 
                
                if (!bestPair) {
                    bestPair = { dist, p: job.priority, rId: r.id, jId: job.id, job };
                } else {
                    if (dist < bestPair.dist) {
                        bestPair = { dist, p: job.priority, rId: r.id, jId: job.id, job };
                    } else if (dist === bestPair.dist) {
                        if (job.priority > bestPair.p) {
                            bestPair = { dist, p: job.priority, rId: r.id, jId: job.id, job };
                        } else if (job.priority === bestPair.p) {
                            if (r.id < bestPair.rId) {
                                bestPair = { dist, p: job.priority, rId: r.id, jId: job.id, job };
                            } else if (r.id === bestPair.rId) {
                                if (job.id < bestPair.jId) {
                                    bestPair = { dist, p: job.priority, rId: r.id, jId: job.id, job };
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        if (!bestPair) break; 
        
        assignments[bestPair.rId].push(bestPair.jId);
        robotPos.set(bestPair.rId, { x: bestPair.job.x, y: bestPair.job.y });
        unassigned.delete(bestPair.job);
    }
    
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ assignments }));
}

solve();

const fs = require('fs');

function solve() {
    const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
    if (!input.trim()) return;
    const data = JSON.parse(input);

    const probability = data.probability;
    const drones = data.drones;
    const maxStepsPerDrone = data.maxStepsPerDrone;

    const R = probability.length;
    if (R === 0) return;
    const C = probability[0].length;

    const paths = drones.map(d => [[d.x, d.y]]);
    const pos = drones.map(d => ({ x: d.x, y: d.y }));

    const visited = Array.from({ length: R }, () => new Array(C).fill(false));
    for (const p of pos) {
        visited[p.y][p.x] = true;
        probability[p.y][p.x] = 0;
    }

    const dx = [0, 1, 0, -1, 0];
    const dy = [-1, 0, 1, 0, 0];

    let lookahead = 5;
    const totalSimulations = maxStepsPerDrone * drones.length;
    if (totalSimulations > 5000) {
        lookahead = 4;
    }
    if (totalSimulations > 20000) {
        lookahead = 3;
    }

    function getBestMove(x, y) {
        let bestMove = 4;
        let maxVal = -1;

        function dfs(cx, cy, steps, currentVal, currentVisited) {
            if (steps === 0) return currentVal;
            let maxSub = currentVal;
            for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
                const nx = cx + dx[i];
                const ny = cy + dy[i];
                if (nx >= 0 && nx < C && ny >= 0 && ny < R && probability[ny][nx] !== -1) {
                    const key = ny * C + nx;
                    const wasVisited = currentVisited.has(key) || visited[ny][nx];
                    const val = wasVisited ? 0 : probability[ny][nx];
                    if (!wasVisited && val > 0) {
                        currentVisited.add(key);
                    }
                    const subVal = dfs(nx, ny, steps - 1, currentVal + val, currentVisited);
                    if (subVal > maxSub) {
                        maxSub = subVal;
                    }
                    if (!wasVisited && val > 0) {
                        currentVisited.delete(key);
                    }
                }
            }
            return maxSub;
        }

        for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
            const nx = x + dx[i];
            const ny = y + dy[i];
            if (nx >= 0 && nx < C && ny >= 0 && ny < R && probability[ny][nx] !== -1) {
                const currentVisited = new Set();
                const key = ny * C + nx;
                currentVisited.add(key);
                const val = visited[ny][nx] ? 0 : probability[ny][nx];
                const score = dfs(nx, ny, lookahead - 1, val, currentVisited);
                if (score > maxVal) {
                    maxVal = score;
                    bestMove = i;
                }
            }
        }
        
        return bestMove;
    }

    for (let step = 0; step < maxStepsPerDrone; step++) {
        for (let d = 0; d < drones.length; d++) {
            const move = getBestMove(pos[d].x, pos[d].y);
            pos[d].x += dx[move];
            pos[d].y += dy[move];
            paths[d].push([pos[d].x, pos[d].y]);
            
            visited[pos[d].y][pos[d].x] = true;
            probability[pos[d].y][pos[d].x] = 0;
        }
    }

    console.log(JSON.stringify({ paths }));
}

solve();

const fs = require('fs');

class PriorityQueue {
    constructor(compare) {
        this.data = [];
        this.compare = compare;
    }
    push(val) {
        this.data.push(val);
        this.up(this.data.length - 1);
    }
    pop() {
        if (this.data.length === 0) return null;
        if (this.data.length === 1) return this.data.pop();
        const top = this.data[0];
        this.data[0] = this.data.pop();
        this.down(0);
        return top;
    }
    up(i) {
        while (i > 0) {
            const p = Math.floor((i - 1) / 2);
            if (this.compare(this.data[i], this.data[p]) < 0) {
                const tmp = this.data[i];
                this.data[i] = this.data[p];
                this.data[p] = tmp;
                i = p;
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    down(i) {
        const n = this.data.length;
        while (true) {
            let left = 2 * i + 1;
            let right = 2 * i + 2;
            let best = i;
            if (left < n && this.compare(this.data[left], this.data[best]) < 0) {
                best = left;
            }
            if (right < n && this.compare(this.data[right], this.data[best]) < 0) {
                best = right;
            }
            if (best !== i) {
                const tmp = this.data[i];
                this.data[i] = this.data[best];
                this.data[best] = tmp;
                i = best;
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    get length() {
        return this.data.length;
    }
}

function solve() {
    const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
    if (!input.trim()) return;
    const data = JSON.parse(input);
    const tasks = data.tasks;
    if (!tasks || tasks.length === 0) {
        console.log(JSON.stringify({ order: [] }));
        return;
    }
    
    const adj = new Map();
    const taskMap = new Map();
    const inDegree = new Map();
    
    for (const t of tasks) {
        taskMap.set(t.id, t);
        adj.set(t.id, []);
        inDegree.set(t.id, 0);
    }
    
    for (const t of tasks) {
        if (t.deps) {
            for (const dep of t.deps) {
                if (!adj.has(dep)) {
                    adj.set(dep, []);
                    inDegree.set(dep, 0);
                }
                adj.get(dep).push(t.id);
                inDegree.set(t.id, (inDegree.get(t.id) || 0) + 1);
            }
        }
    }
    
    const bottomLevel = new Map();
    function getBottomLevel(u) {
        if (bottomLevel.has(u)) return bottomLevel.get(u);
        let maxV = 0;
        const neighbors = adj.get(u) || [];
        for (const v of neighbors) {
            maxV = Math.max(maxV, getBottomLevel(v));
        }
        const t = taskMap.get(u);
        const val = (t ? t.duration : 0) + maxV;
        bottomLevel.set(u, val);
        return val;
    }
    
    for (const t of tasks) {
        getBottomLevel(t.id);
    }
    
    const compare = (a, b) => {
        const ta = taskMap.get(a);
        const tb = taskMap.get(b);
        const bla = bottomLevel.get(a);
        const blb = bottomLevel.get(b);
        
        if (bla !== blb) return blb - bla; // descending bottom level
        
        const da = ta && ta.deadline !== undefined ? ta.deadline : Infinity;
        const db = tb && tb.deadline !== undefined ? tb.deadline : Infinity;
        if (da !== db) return da - db; // ascending deadline
        
        const wa = ta && ta.weight !== undefined ? ta.weight : 0;
        const wb = tb && tb.weight !== undefined ? tb.weight : 0;
        if (wa !== wb) return wb - wa; // descending weight
        
        return a.localeCompare ? a.localeCompare(b) : (a < b ? -1 : (a > b ? 1 : 0));
    };
    
    const pq = new PriorityQueue(compare);
    
    for (const t of tasks) {
        if (inDegree.get(t.id) === 0) {
            pq.push(t.id);
        }
    }
    
    const order = [];
    while (pq.length > 0) {
        const nxt = pq.pop();
        order.push(nxt);
        
        const neighbors = adj.get(nxt) || [];
        for (const v of neighbors) {
            const ind = inDegree.get(v) - 1;
            inDegree.set(v, ind);
            if (ind === 0) {
                pq.push(v);
            }
        }
    }
    
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ order: order }));
}

declare const require: any; 
const fs = require('fs'); 
const input: string = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
const data = JSON.parse(input);

const depot = data.depot;
const packages = data.packages;
const n = packages.length;

if (n === 0) {
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ routes: [] }));
    process.exit(0);
}

const xs = new Float64Array(n);
const ys = new Float64Array(n);
for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    xs[i] = packages[i].x;
    ys[i] = packages[i].y;
}
const depotX = depot[0];
const depotY = depot[1];

let unvisited = new Uint8Array(n);
unvisited.fill(1);

let currentX = depotX;
let currentY = depotY;
let tour = new Int32Array(n);

// 1. Nearest Neighbor Initialization
for (let step = 0; step < n; step++) {
    let bestIdx = -1;
    let bestDist = Infinity;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (unvisited[i]) {
            const dx = currentX - xs[i];
            const dy = currentY - ys[i];
            const d = dx * dx + dy * dy;
            if (d < bestDist) {
                bestDist = d;
                bestIdx = i;
            }
        }
    }
    tour[step] = bestIdx;
    unvisited[bestIdx] = 0;
    currentX = xs[bestIdx];
    currentY = ys[bestIdx];
}

// 2. 2-opt Refinement
let improvement = true;
let passes = 0;
const MAX_PASSES = 50;
const start_time = Date.now();

while (improvement && passes < MAX_PASSES) {
    if (Date.now() - start_time > 8000) break; // 8-second time limit to ensure fast termination
    improvement = false;
    passes++;
    
    for (let i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) {
        const x_i_minus_1 = i === 0 ? depotX : xs[tour[i - 1]];
        const y_i_minus_1 = i === 0 ? depotY : ys[tour[i - 1]];
        const x_i = xs[tour[i]];
        const y_i = ys[tour[i]];
        
        for (let k = i + 1; k < n; k++) {
            const x_k = xs[tour[k]];
            const y_k = ys[tour[k]];
            const x_k_plus_1 = k === n - 1 ? depotX : xs[tour[k + 1]];
            const y_k_plus_1 = k === n - 1 ? depotY : ys[tour[k + 1]];
            
            const dx1 = x_i_minus_1 - x_i;
            const dy1 = y_i_minus_1 - y_i;
            const d1 = Math.sqrt(dx1*dx1 + dy1*dy1);
            
            const dx2 = x_k - x_k_plus_1;
            const dy2 = y_k - y_k_plus_1;
            const d2 = Math.sqrt(dx2*dx2 + dy2*dy2);
            
            const dx3 = x_i_minus_1 - x_k;
            const dy3 = y_i_minus_1 - y_k;
            const d3 = Math.sqrt(dx3*dx3 + dy3*dy3);
            
            const dx4 = x_i - x_k_plus_1;
            const dy4 = y_i - y_k_plus_1;
            const d4 = Math.sqrt(dx4*dx4 + dy4*dy4);
            
            if (d3 + d4 < d1 + d2 - 1e-9) {
                let left = i;
                let right = k;
                while (left < right) {
                    let temp = tour[left];
                    tour[left] = tour[right];
                    tour[right] = temp;
                    left++;
                    right--;
                }
                improvement = true;
                break; 
            }
        }
    }
}

// 3. Output Preparation
const routeIds = [];
for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    routeIds.push(packages[tour[i]].id);
}

console.log(JSON.stringify({ routes: [routeIds] }));

declare const require: any;
const fs = require('fs');

function solve() {
    const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
    const data = JSON.parse(input);
    const { width, height, grid, ignitions, towns, cutBudget } = data;

    if (cutBudget === 0) {
        console.log(JSON.stringify({ firebreaks: [] }));
        return;
    }

    const isBurnable = new Uint8Array(width * height);
    const isTown = new Uint8Array(width * height);
    let totalTownValue = 0;
    
    for (let y = 0; y < height; y++) {
        for (let x = 0; x < width; x++) {
            if (grid[y][x] === '.') {
                isBurnable[y * width + x] = 1;
            }
        }
    }

    for (const t of towns) {
        isTown[t.y * width + t.x] = 1;
        totalTownValue += t.value;
    }
    
    // We cannot cut ignition cells
    for (const ig of ignitions) {
        isBurnable[ig[1] * width + ig[0]] = 0;
    }
    // We shouldn't cut town cells
    for (const t of towns) {
        isBurnable[t.y * width + t.x] = 0;
    }

    let candidates: number[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < width * height; i++) {
        if (isBurnable[i]) candidates.push(i);
    }

    function evaluate(cuts: number[]): number {
        const burned = new Uint8Array(width * height);
        const q = new Int32Array(width * height);
        let head = 0;
        let tail = 0;

        for (const ig of ignitions) {
            const idx = ig[1] * width + ig[0];
            burned[idx] = 1;
            q[tail++] = idx;
        }

        const cutSet = new Uint8Array(width * height);
        for (let i = 0; i < cuts.length; i++) cutSet[cuts[i]] = 1;

        while (head < tail) {
            const curr = q[head++];
            const cx = curr % width;
            const cy = Math.floor(curr / width);

            const neighbors = [
                curr - width, // up
                curr + width, // down
                curr - 1,     // left
                curr + 1      // right
            ];

            if (cy === 0) neighbors[0] = -1;
            if (cy === height - 1) neighbors[1] = -1;
            if (cx === 0) neighbors[2] = -1;
            if (cx === width - 1) neighbors[3] = -1;

            for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
                const n = neighbors[i];
                if (n >= 0 && !burned[n] && !cutSet[n] && (grid[Math.floor(n/width)][n%width] === '.' || isTown[n])) {
                    burned[n] = 1;
                    q[tail++] = n;
                }
            }
        }

        let savedValue = 0;
        for (const t of towns) {
            if (!burned[t.y * width + t.x]) {
                savedValue += t.value;
            }
        }
        return savedValue;
    }

    let bestCuts: number[] = [];
    let bestScore = -1;

    // Simple randomized hill climbing
    const tStart = Date.now();
    let currentCuts: number[] = [];
    
    // Initialize with random valid candidates
    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(cutBudget, candidates.length); i++) {
        let r = Math.floor(Math.random() * candidates.length);
        currentCuts.push(candidates[r]);
    }

    bestCuts = [...currentCuts];
    bestScore = evaluate(currentCuts);
    let currentScore = bestScore;

    let iters = 0;
    while (Date.now() - tStart < 8000) {
        iters++;
        if (currentCuts.length === 0) break;
        
        const replaceIdx = Math.floor(Math.random() * currentCuts.length);
        const oldCut = currentCuts[replaceIdx];
        const newCut = candidates[Math.floor(Math.random() * candidates.length)];
        
        currentCuts[replaceIdx] = newCut;
        const score = evaluate(currentCuts);
        
        if (score >= currentScore) {
            currentScore = score;
            if (score > bestScore) {
                bestScore = score;
                bestCuts = [...currentCuts];
            }
        } else {
            // Revert
            currentCuts[replaceIdx] = oldCut;
        }
    }

    const firebreaks = bestCuts.map(idx => [idx % width, Math.floor(idx / width)]);
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ firebreaks }));
}

solve();

declare const require: any;
const fs = require('fs');

function solve() {
    const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
    const data = JSON.parse(input);
    
    const prob: number[][] = data.probability;
    const height = prob.length;
    const width = prob[0].length;
    const maxSteps = data.maxStepsPerDrone;
    const drones: {id: any, x: number, y: number}[] = data.drones;
    
    const visited = new Set<string>();
    
    const paths: [number, number][][] = [];
    for (const d of drones) {
        paths.push([[d.x, d.y]]);
        visited.add(`${d.x},${d.y}`);
    }
    
    const dx = [0, 1, 0, -1, 0];
    const dy = [1, 0, -1, 0, 0];
    
    const currPos = drones.map(d => ({x: d.x, y: d.y}));
    
    // To avoid multiple drones targeting the same far away cell simultaneously
    const claimed = new Set<string>();
    
    for (let step = 0; step < maxSteps; step++) {
        for (let i = 0; i < drones.length; i++) {
            const pos = currPos[i];
            
            let bestTarget: {x: number, y: number} | null = null;
            let bestScore = -1;
            let bestTargetKey = "";
            
            const q: {x: number, y: number, dist: number, fx: number, fy: number}[] = [];
            const bfsVisited = new Set<string>();
            
            for (let dir = 0; dir < 5; dir++) {
                const nx = pos.x + dx[dir];
                const ny = pos.y + dy[dir];
                if (nx >= 0 && nx < width && ny >= 0 && ny < height && prob[ny][nx] !== -1) {
                    q.push({x: nx, y: ny, dist: 1, fx: nx, fy: ny});
                    bfsVisited.add(`${nx},${ny}`);
                }
            }
            
            let qIdx = 0;
            const maxBfsDepth = 20;
            
            while (qIdx < q.length) {
                const curr = q[qIdx++];
                
                if (curr.dist > maxBfsDepth) break;
                
                const key = `${curr.x},${curr.y}`;
                if (!visited.has(key) && !claimed.has(key) && prob[curr.y][curr.x] > 0) {
                    const score = prob[curr.y][curr.x] / (curr.dist * curr.dist);
                    if (score > bestScore) {
                        bestScore = score;
                        bestTarget = {x: curr.fx, y: curr.fy};
                        bestTargetKey = key;
                    }
                }
                
                if (curr.dist < maxBfsDepth) {
                    for (let dir = 0; dir < 4; dir++) {
                        const nx = curr.x + dx[dir];
                        const ny = curr.y + dy[dir];
                        if (nx >= 0 && nx < width && ny >= 0 && ny < height && prob[ny][nx] !== -1) {
                            const nkey = `${nx},${ny}`;
                            if (!bfsVisited.has(nkey)) {
                                bfsVisited.add(nkey);
                                q.push({x: nx, y: ny, dist: curr.dist + 1, fx: curr.fx, fy: curr.fy});
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            
            if (bestTarget) {
                pos.x = bestTarget.x;
                pos.y = bestTarget.y;
                if (bestTargetKey !== `${pos.x},${pos.y}`) {
                    claimed.add(bestTargetKey); // claim it so others don't go for it
                }
            } else {
                // If no target found, just pick any valid unvisited neighbor, or just valid
                let moved = false;
                for (let dir = 0; dir < 4; dir++) {
                    const nx = pos.x + dx[dir];
                    const ny = pos.y + dy[dir];
                    if (nx >= 0 && nx < width && ny >= 0 && ny < height && prob[ny][nx] !== -1) {
                        const key = `${nx},${ny}`;
                        if (!visited.has(key)) {
                            pos.x = nx;
                            pos.y = ny;
                            moved = true;
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                }
                if (!moved) {
                    for (let dir = 0; dir < 5; dir++) {
                        const nx = pos.x + dx[dir];
                        const ny = pos.y + dy[dir];
                        if (nx >= 0 && nx < width && ny >= 0 && ny < height && prob[ny][nx] !== -1) {
                            pos.x = nx;
                            pos.y = ny;
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            
            paths[i].push([pos.x, pos.y]);
            visited.add(`${pos.x},${pos.y}`);
        }
        claimed.clear(); // Clear claims each step to allow re-evaluating
    }
    
    console.log(JSON.stringify({paths}));
}

solve();

declare const require: any;
const fs = require('fs');

function solve() {
    const input: string = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8');
    const data = JSON.parse(input);

    const tasks: any[] = data.tasks;

    const outEdges = new Map<string | number, (string | number)[]>();
    const taskMap = new Map<string | number, any>();
    const inDegree = new Map<string | number, number>();

    for (const t of tasks) {
        taskMap.set(t.id, t);
        inDegree.set(t.id, t.deps ? t.deps.length : 0);
        if (!outEdges.has(t.id)) outEdges.set(t.id, []);
    }

    for (const t of tasks) {
        if (t.deps) {
            for (const dep of t.deps) {
                if (!outEdges.has(dep)) outEdges.set(dep, []);
                outEdges.get(dep)!.push(t.id);
            }
        }
    }

    const reverseInDegree = new Map<string | number, number>();
    for (const t of tasks) {
        reverseInDegree.set(t.id, outEdges.get(t.id)!.length);
    }

    const revAvailable: (string | number)[] = [];
    for (const t of tasks) {
        if (reverseInDegree.get(t.id) === 0) {
            revAvailable.push(t.id);
        }
    }

    const revOrder: (string | number)[] = [];
    let head = 0;
    while (head < revAvailable.length) {
        const curr = revAvailable[head++];
        revOrder.push(curr);
        const t = taskMap.get(curr)!;
        if (t.deps) {
            for (const dep of t.deps) {
                const d = reverseInDegree.get(dep)! - 1;
                reverseInDegree.set(dep, d);
                if (d === 0) {
                    revAvailable.push(dep);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    const memo = new Map<string | number, number>();
    for (const id of revOrder) {
        let maxChild = 0;
        const children = outEdges.get(id) || [];
        for (const child of children) {
            maxChild = Math.max(maxChild, memo.get(child) || 0);
        }
        memo.set(id, taskMap.get(id)!.duration + maxChild);
    }

    const available: any[] = [];
    for (const t of tasks) {
        if (inDegree.get(t.id) === 0) {
            available.push(t);
        }
    }

    const order: (string | number)[] = [];

    while (available.length > 0) {
        let bestIdx = 0;
        let bestScore = -Infinity;

        for (let i = 0; i < available.length; i++) {
            const t = available[i];
            const bl = memo.get(t.id)!;
            
            let score = bl;
            score += (t.weight * 1000) / (t.deadline > 0 ? t.deadline : 1);
            
            if (score > bestScore) {
                bestScore = score;
                bestIdx = i;
            }
        }

        const nextTask = available[bestIdx];
        available[bestIdx] = available[available.length - 1];
        available.pop();
        order.push(nextTask.id);

        const children = outEdges.get(nextTask.id) || [];
        for (const child of children) {
            const deg = inDegree.get(child)! - 1;
            inDegree.set(child, deg);
            if (deg === 0) {
                available.push(taskMap.get(child)!);
            }
        }
    }

    console.log(JSON.stringify({ order }));
}

solve();
